title: Jelly Roll's daughter fiercely denies cheating rumors, days after divorce from Bunnie Xo finalized
content: Jelly Roll's daughter fiercely defended her family, days after his divorce from Bunnie Xo was finalized. Bailee Ann, 18, staunchly denied infidelity rumors between the former couple during a TikTok livestream Sunday. The "Son of a Sinner" singer petitioned Tennessee courts for a divorce May 18, according to documents obtained by Fox News Digital. A judge finalized the end to their marriage Friday. JELLY ROLL, BUNNIE XO HINTED AT DIVORCE WEEKS BEFORE THE NEWS BROKE WITH CRYPTIC LYRICS AND MISSING RINGS He listed the date of separation as May 9 and cited irreconcilable differences. "Nobody cheated," Bailee said on the livestream, according to People . "Period. [Get] the f--- out of my comments, my DMs, my live with that s---, I don’t care, I don’t want to talk about it." She told her followers they had "no f---ing idea what happened, and wait ‘til y’all find out," before threatening that "the internet in totality is about to f---ing crumble the day that I open my mouth." BUNNIE XO SAYS SHE FUNDED JELLY ROLL'S EARLY CAREER BY 'TURNING TRICKS' WHILE REFLECTING ON DIVORCE "It’s not a difference in f---ing opinions," she said. "Nobody else lived in it. So don’t f---ing even. I’m for real so done. Good? Everybody good? We’re on the same page? Cool." Bunnie Xo and Jelly Roll (born Jason DeFord) have fiercely defended their private relationship after news of their split broke the internet with accusations of cheating. Terms of their settlement remain confidential. However, People reported the former couple will split their assets, including homes, cars, an aircraft and any intellectual property. Additionally, the "Save Me" singer will make a "one-time, confidential lump sum payment to Bunnie, so there will be no alimony claims to be made in court," the outlet reported. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER Bunnie, who's full name is Alisa DeFord, recently gave her social media followers a tour of her new Nashville-area home, which included hidden stairways, multiple massive closets, opulent floral rooms, an outdoor shower and an infinity pool. Of the many topics discussed in her since-scrubbed "divorce" podcast episode, Bunnie admitted her past life as a high-end escort funded their lifestyle when they first dated. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "When Jay and I first got together, we were two kids who literally had nothing," Bunnie said of her ex. "Everybody always likes to say that I had all the money when we first got together, and I did this for him and I did that for him. And, I mean, I had sugar daddies at the time that were paying for all of this." "Like, we have — and I'm not trying to take the, the light off of what I did for him — but, like, we were still in the streets. We were making money as it came. "It wasn't like I was over here just sitting on f---ing a million dollars and was taking care of him. Like, I was turning tricks to pay our bills and to get lawyers and to travel and to, you know, go on tour and stuff like that." title: Alleged 'mime' stalker stripped to underwear, covered himself in cooking oil: officials
content: Not all mimes stay silent. One is now accused of terrorizing women. A Massachusetts man known for roaming in a black-and-white mime costume is accused of frightening women for months at a popular state park, where prosecutors say he allegedly stripped to his underwear, slathered himself in cooking oil and worked out near female employees before later collapsing in court as the allegations were read aloud. Hernan Villagran Lux, 29, of Framingham, is facing criminal harassment charges after three female state Department of Conservation and Recreation (DCR) employees had up to over 50 encounters over the past two months at a Natick state park near Boston. Prosecutors said all three women knew Lux by name and appearance, and one reported more than 50 encounters that authorities said escalated over time, eventually leaving employees afraid to work around him. FLORIDA MAN WHO ALLEGEDLY LURED WOMEN WITH DATING APP COULD HAVE MORE VICTIMS: AUTHORITIES The allegations have also sparked warnings on social media, where people across several Massachusetts communities said they recognized the suspect and claimed he had approached or followed women on a nearby rail trail. Authorities arrested Lux Sunday night on the Cochituate Rail Trail, after multiple women and park workers alleged he repeatedly approached them, stared at them and refused to leave despite repeated requests, according to Boston 25 News . "The women report an extensive number of contacts with the defendant involving him staring at them, smiling in what they describe as 'a really unnerving and frankly terrifying manner,'" Framingham District Court Supervisor Andrew Mange said during Monday's court hearing. MAN ACCUSED OF REPEATEDLY TRESPASSING AT CIA HEADQUARTERS IN VIRGINIA Mange said the encounters became increasingly bold. In one incident, prosecutors allege Lux "stripped down to his underwear, slathered cooking oil all over his body and began working out right by their staff area." The women also reported that Lux repeatedly refused to leave the park after being asked to do so, according to the station. Prosecutors also alleged Lux complimented one employee's appearance, commented on her lips and refused to leave as she and coworkers abandoned their work area because they felt unsafe. Boston 25 reported that numerous people posted on social media saying they had spotted a man matching Lux's distinctive mime-like appearance throughout Framingham, Natick and Wayland. Several women also claimed a man fitting the same description approached and followed them on the Cochituate Rail Trail. "I spotted him, he looked kind of odd but I thought he was just dressed in a costume," neighbor Nancy Dlott told Boston 25. "It's kind of upsetting, especially if you're walking alone," she added. "I just don't understand what goes through someone's head to do that," Christopher Labella told the station. "I hope this guy gets the help that he needs." As prosecutors continued reading the allegations in court Monday, Lux fainted and was treated before proceedings resumed, according to Boston 25. When court resumed later in the afternoon, the judge ordered Lux to undergo a mental health evaluation at Bridgewater State Hospital.

title: U.S. measles cases surpass last year's total: Tracker
content: The U.S. measles case count for this year has surged past last year's total and now stands at 2,295 — a level that hasn't been seen in 35 years, according to a Johns Hopkins University tracker that compiles state and local health data. Why it matters: It's the latest sign that the virus is rebounding in areas with low vaccine coverage, threatening the United States' measles elimination status , which is due to be reviewed in November. The big picture : The majority of cases are in unvaccinated people. While overall measles vaccination rates are still relatively high, public health officials say they must remain above 95% to maintain herd immunity. By the numbers: As of Tuesday, there were nine more cases than all of 2025 , per the Johns Hopkins U.S. measles tracker. Jurisdictions including South Carolina, Utah, Texas, Florida and Arizona have the most reported cases. The Centers for Disease Control reported 2,260 confirmed cases in its last update on July 16. The agency said there were 34 new outbreaks reported this year. The last time measles cases were higher was in 1991, when the U.S. had 9,643 cases, according to CDC data . Threat level: Measles symptoms include a cough, high fever and conjunctivitis as well as a telltale rash, but can escalate into complications such as severe ear infections, pneumonia and encephalitis or inflammation of the brain that can lead to permanent brain damage and even death, per Johns Hopkins Medicine. On average, measles kills between one and three of every 1,000 infected children. The rebound comes at a time when a number of key top government health positions — including CDC director and surgeon general — remain vacant and after Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. initially downplayed the virus' threat. He's since said the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine is the most effective way to prevent measles spread while noting vaccination is a personal choice.

title: 'Jumping ship': House Dem finds exit strategy after SCOTUS ruling shifts advantage to GOP
content: Democratic Rep. Cleo Fields of Louisiana announced Tuesday he will not seek re-election to Congress after a Supreme Court ruling and new Louisiana congressional map reshaped his district in Republicans’ favor. Fields said in a statement announcing his plans he will instead run to fill the unexpired term for the state Senate in Louisiana’s 14th District, saying he feels his "calling to serve the people is better put to use back home than here in D.C." "I intend to answer that call," Fields added. LOUISIANA SUSPENDS CONGRESSIONAL PRIMARIES IN WAKE OF SUPREME COURT GERRYMANDERING RULING Fields is seeking to return to the state Senate seat he held before winning election to Congress in 2024. State Sen. Larry Selders won a 2025 special election to fill the vacancy Fields left, but his death earlier this month opened up the seat once again. The National Republican Congressional Committee took advantage of the announcement, arguing Fields was "jumping ship" shortly after the committee added Louisiana’s 6th Congressional District to its target list. The NRCC announced Monday that LA-06 was among seven additional Democratic-held seats it was targeting, saying President Donald Trump carried the newly drawn district by 32.1 points in 2024. SUPREME COURT RULES ON KEY VOTING RIGHTS ACT RULE AS REPUBLICANS AND DEMOCRATS WAGE REDISTRICTING WAR Fields has had a long career in elected office, first being elected to the Louisiana State Senate in 1987, then running for Congress unsuccessfully in 1990. Fields tried again and eventually joined Congress in 1992, during which he also ran for governor and lost. Fields left Congress after two terms, returned to the state senate for a decade and then was elected back to Congress in 2024 after a prior congressional redistricting effort created a second majority-Black district. The current redistricting fight in Louisiana dates back to the state’s post-2020 census map, which included one majority-Black congressional district before a federal court found the map likely violated the Voting Rights Act and ordered the state to add a second. Louisiana lawmakers then adopted a 2024 map that turned Fields’ 6th Congressional District into a second majority-Black seat favorable to Democrats, but the Supreme Court later ruled in Louisiana v. Callais that the district was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander, prompting state lawmakers to approve new lines that reduced the state back to one majority-Black district and five Republican-favored districts.

title: World Cup hero Ferran Torres doubles down after criticism, posts picture wearing 'Make Spain Great Again' hat
content: The 2026 FIFA World Cup , the most successful tournament in the organization's history, recently came to a close with Spain beating Argentina in extra time to win their second ever title. It was the culmination of a remarkable defensive performance from the Spanish national team, a run where they allowed just one goal throughout the tournament. Despite facing Belgium, arguably the most talented roster in the world, France, and Argentina with one of the best goal scorers in history, Lionel Messi. But it wasn't one of their defenders that grabbed headlines afterward, it was the Cup-winning goal scorer Ferran Torres. Torres after the match said that he felt the goal was the result of support from the Spanish population. SPAIN BEATS ARGENTINA TO WIN 2026 FIFA WORLD CUP BEHIND FERRAN TORRES' EXTRA-TIME GOAL "I think in the end the goal came from 47 million people [the estimated Spain population], not just those of us that are here," Torres said to FIFA broadcasters after the win, per ESPN . "Today destiny was written, it was made for us to win. We’re far from our people today but we tried to be as close as possible to them." Then, during the parade, he was photographed wearing a red "Make Spain Great Again" hat, in an apparent reference to President Donald Trump 's "Make America Great Again" slogan. Criticism from the political left was, predictably, swift and intense. The deputy spokesman for the left-wing "Sumar" group in Spain immediately accused Torres of speculating in real estate, as just one example. The progressive media outlet El Plural said his hat was a "clear ideological message, provoking a multitude of criticism" on social media. FERRAN TORRES SPORTS 'MAKE SPAIN GREAT AGAIN' HAT SIMILAR TO TRUMP'S SLOGAN AT WORLD CUP HOMECOMING PARADE Well, Torres either didn't hear the criticism or didn't care, because in a new post on X from Tuesday evening, he posted several photos from the parade, prominently featuring the hat. The caption, "Somos los reyessssss! Vaya locura!," roughly translates to "We are the kings! It's absolutely crazy!" CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM It's still unclear whether Torres meant to wear the hat as a nod to right-wing causes in Spain, as an attempt to mock Trump, or whether it was just a fun nod to the fact that the president presented the trophy to the national team. Though it does seem that most left-leaning commentators and politicians took it as a statement of support for reforming the country, which is currently under the control of a far-left socialist government led by Pedro Sanchez. A YouGov poll in June found that Sanchez had just a 33% approval rating, with 63% holding unfavorable views. Perhaps this was a result of his plan to give residence permits to illegal immigrants in Spain. Which, given Trump's stance on immigration enforcement , seemingly, aligns with the "MSGA" hat. Regardless, it's telling that the Barcelona star has made no apology for wearing it, despite the criticism.

title: Mamdani says even if he can get along with Trump, he still demands that 'ICE should be abolished'
content: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani spoke to Rolling Stone for an interview published Tuesday about how he and President Donald Trump can agree on a shared love of New York, but they are sharply divided about ICE. After widespread media concern about the rise of Mayor-elect Zohran Mamdani, he shocked the nation by having a surprisingly chummy meeting with Trump after months of wary rhetoric from both politicians. In one viral moment, Trump gracefully shrugged off a reporter asking Mamdani about his past comments of Trump being a fascist, saying he doesn’t care. A Rolling Stone interviewer marveled at this as he spoke to Mamdani , saying, "I think that was kind of one of the most striking parts of the very beginning of your tenure as mayor was that meeting with Trump at the White House that went, I think to pretty much any observer, really well for both of you. He probably felt the same way. MAMDANI DESCRIBES TRUMP RELATIONSHIP AS 'HONEST' AND 'DIRECT' AMID RECENT BLOWOUT "What's your current relationship now?" "The relationship is as it was. It's built around New York City ," Mamdani said. "I think for all of the many disagreements that the president and I have, we have one thing in common, which is a love of this place. And whenever we speak, whenever we meet, it always comes back to that." The interviewer recalled recent controversies when ICE performed widespread raids in America’s major cities, asking the mayor whether he tries to stay on Trump’s good side to prevent a similarly scaled mass deportation raid in New York City. TOM HOMAN WARNS ICE SURGE COMING TO NEW YORK CITY AS MAMDANI BOASTS ABOUT SANCTUARY STATUS "I think I need to continue to be honest with the president, and that honesty is in places of disagreement," Mamdani replied. "I've spoken to him directly about how I think of ICE as a cruel agency that does nothing to serve the interests of public safety. And I've spoken about how I think that ICE should be abolished . We should have an immigration system that has humanity at the heart of it. "And, also, the president, he is a New Yorker. In that first meeting, as much as we were having a conversation as the mayor and the president, we were also having a conversation as two New Yorkers, even at one point talking about community boards and zoning laws." title: Stephen A Smith says he confronted ESPN bosses over Ryan Clark firing: 'I am not happy'
content: Stephen A. Smith is blowing his top after ESPN cold-bloodedly axed his friend, Ryan Clark. OutKick first confirmed the details of Clark's exit, revealing that executives pulled the plug on the Super Bowl champion while he was actively co-hosting "NFL Live" on live television. After learning The Mothership had tossed his broadcast partner into the corporate meat grinder, Smith went straight to his YouTube show and let it rip. ESPN PARTING WAYS WITH NFL ANALYST RYAN CLARK AHEAD OF NETWORK'S FIRST SUPER BOWL BROADCAST "My brother, Ryan Clark, a person that I consider to be arguably the best NFL analyst in America, is no longer a member of ESPN," a visibly distraught Smith told his online audience. "And I can't even tell y'all how much that hurts." Network brass originally planned to notify the gridiron star on Tuesday. However, after OutKick's very own Dan Zaksheske and Bobby Burack contacted ESPN PR about an impending story detailing the dismissal, executives rushed to yank Clark off the broadcast so he would not read about his firing on social media. EXCLUSIVE: ESPN TO PART WAYS WITH CAM NEWTON AS PART OF TALENT LAYOFFS THAT ALSO INCLUDED RYAN CLARK Smith revealed that Bristol management actually approached him before pulling the trigger on Clark. Yet, despite Smith being the ratings magnet on the network, his pleas to protect his colleague were ignored. "Was I asked what I thought what my feelings were? Yes, I was," Smith admitted during his stream. "Of course I said we have to keep them. But I don't get to make those decisions. And I don't get to ignore the fiscal and financial circumstances and ultimate ramifications that come with the job." Smith made it clear that he confronted top bosses directly. ESPN LOSES SOLE EXECUTIVE WHO CRACKED DOWN ON POLITICAL, RACIAL RHETORIC "I am not happy about this decision one bit. The bosses know I am not happy about this decision," Smith declared. "I've made that very, very clear. The only thing that I can definitively say to you is that there's nobody that's going to be let go that was more of a friend and a brother to me than Ryan Clark." "When I saw how people were talking about him, I was like, 'They don't know him at all,'" Smith fumed. "He was conscientious and thoughtful." Even as he voiced his disapproval, Smith conceded that executives operating at the direction of parent company Disney ultimately answer to the bottom line. "Decisions like this, I would imagine, don't come easy. They have to be made... Business is business," Smith acknowledged. "It's Tuesday, and by the end of the day you're going to hear about a lot more folks getting laid off. For all I know, some of my friends are going to be gone." Clark's tenure at ESPN also came with no shortage of controversy. He drew backlash for comments following Charlie Kirk's assassination, came under scrutiny for his handling of Kyren Lacy's death , and sparred on air with fellow analyst Peter Schrager, dismissing him as a "non-player." SAS signed off his broadcast with an emotional personal message directly to his ousted partner. "Love you bro, you know that. Always, always here," Smith said. "Talk to you soon." title: Mamdani goes back on campaign promise, says NYC can't arrest Netanyahu
content: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani acknowledged Tuesday that he can't have Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu arrested despite promising to do so during his mayoral campaign. But he called on the federal government to execute an International Criminal Court's arrest warrant if the Israeli leader visits New York. In a video posted on X, Mamdani called Netanyahu a "war criminal" while conceding that New York City could not enforce the ICC warrant on its own. "As I've said, I agree with the ICC that Benjamin Netanyahu should be arrested and tried for his crimes, as I do for anyone else charged by the ICC," Mamdani said. NETANYAHU FIRES BACK AT NYC MAYOR MAMDANI'S VOW TO ENFORCE 'BOGUS ARREST WARRANT' "My administration has reviewed every avenue available under applicable law to determine whether New York City could execute the International Criminal Court's arrest warrant if Benjamin Netanyahu came here," he continued. "It is clear that we do not have the independent legal authority to enforce this warrant. The federal government, however, does, and I call on them to join the ICC and execute this warrant." Mamdani's comments underscored that a New York City mayor lacks the authority to enforce an International Criminal Court warrant or create a New York arrest warrant by executive order. Mamdani nonetheless said Netanyahu would not be welcome in New York City. MAMDANI’S ‘DERANGED’ ISRAEL TAKE RESURFACES AS HE TARGETS NETANYAHU "I want to be equally clear: Benjamin Netanyahu is not welcome in New York City, nor is any other war criminal at large," he said. The remarks marked a reversal from Mamdani's 2025 campaign pledge that New York City would arrest Netanyahu if the Israeli prime minister came to New York. Mamdani's comments came two days after he told The New York Times that the city's Law Department was reviewing whether New York had the legal authority to arrest Netanyahu if he visited the city. TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TOUTS MORE THAN $1B IN UN BUDGET CUTS AS REFORM PUSH GAINS MOMENTUM Netanyahu is expected to travel to New York in September for the United Nations General Assembly. "I believe that Prime Minister Netanyahu belongs in The Hague," Mamdani told the Times. "He's a war criminal who has been charged by the International Criminal Court." Netanyahu's office dismissed the comments Sunday, calling the ICC a "kangaroo court" with "no jurisdiction over Americans or Israelis." "Instead of backing Khan's criminal behaviour, Mr. Mamdani should focus on fixing the damage his policies have caused New York," Netanyahu's office said. The ICC issued arrest warrants for Netanyahu and former Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant in November 2024 over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity tied to Israel's military campaign in Gaza. Fox News Digital has reached out to the Justice Department and Netanyahu's office for comment. Fox News Digital's Ashley J. DiMella, Eric Mack and Jasmine Baehr contributed to this report.

title: Trump approves nuclear agreement that may allow Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium, two AP sources say
content: President Donald Trump gestures while meeting with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun in the Oval Office at the White House, Tuesday, July 21, 2026, in Washington. (AP Photo/Mark Schiefelbein) 2026-07-22T01:42:01Z President Donald Trump has approved an agreement with Saudi Arabia that could potentially provide the kingdom with uranium enrichment capability for its civilian nuclear program, according to two people familiar with the matter. The people, who were not authorized to comment publicly about the yet to be formally announced decision, said the agreement is expected to be announced publicly as early as Wednesday. The deal is expected to last 30 years and is also expected to involve U.S. firms in developing the program. The deal could allow for the building of a uranium enrichment facility in Saudi Arabia following a joint U.S.-Saudi study. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the decision, which was first reported on by the Wall Street Journal.

title: Panthers' Taylor Moton moved to non-football injury list with blood clot as offensive line concerns grow
content: For the first time in a decade, the Carolina Panthers returned to the top of the NFC South. Their breakthrough season ended in January with a home wild-card thriller, where they pushed Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams to the brink. After picking up Bryce Young’s fifth-year option and adding key pieces across the roster, the Panthers enter 2026 with higher expectations as the team eyes a second consecutive division title. But Carolina’s offensive line took another hit Tuesday, creating the latest test for a unit charged with protecting the former No. 1 overall pick. Taylor Moton, the Panthers veteran starting right tackle, will be sidelined when the regular season kicks off in September. Moton learned in late June that doctors had discovered a blood clot in his left lung. The Panthers confirmed on Tuesday that the 31-year-old will miss the start of the season. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM Moton’s setback comes with starting left tackle Ikem Ekwonu still recovering from a ruptured patellar tendon in his right knee. Ekwonu suffered the injury during the Panthers’ playoff game. Ekwonu underwent emergency appendectomy surgery last August. BRONCOS STAR QUARTERBACK BO NIX UNDERWENT SECOND PROCEDURE ON SURGICALLY REPAIRED ANKLE: REPORT Moton was moved to the non-football injury list, joining two-time Pro Bowl defensive back Jaycee Horn. The cornerback missed a Week 12 game against the San Francisco 49ers last season but finished the year with 16 game appearances. Horn landed on the non-football injury list this week after cutting his foot while running, according to the Panthers. After the diagnosis, Moton was put on blood thinners and the team said he has responded well to the treatment. Carolina’s medical staff continues to monitor the veteran lineman day-to-day. The Panthers had already moved to protect themselves on the left side, signing veteran tackle Rasheed Walker in March as a potential replacement for Ekwonu. Moton’s absence could now create an opening on the right side for Monroe Freeling, the offensive tackle Carolina selected with the No. 18 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. The Panthers wasted little time addressing the left side of the offensive line, signing Rasheed Walker in March as insurance for Ekwonu. The next month, Carolina doubled down up front by selecting Monroe Freeling in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft. The Panthers selected Moton in the second round of the 2017 NFL Draft out of Western Michigan. He has spent all nine seasons of his NFL career with Carolina. title: Canada reportedly scraps joint bridge celebration with US after Trump renews tariff threat
content: Canada on Tuesday called off a joint celebration with the United States to mark the opening of the Gordie Howe International Bridge, following renewed tariff threats from President Donald Trump. The bridge — which connects Detroit and Windsor , Ontario — was named after legendary Canadian hockey player Gordie Howe who played for the Detroit Red Wings, symbolizing the longstanding relationship between the two countries. Trump on Monday announced plans to impose a 50% tariff on certain Canadian imports, citing what officials called trade discrimination against American companies in the dairy, auto and alcohol industries. The White House said Canada’s policies gave foreign competitors an unfair advantage. "In light of trade action threatened by the United States earlier this week, it would be inappropriate to proceed with a celebratory event ​between the two countries," Jenna Ghassabeh, a spokesperson for Canadian ​Infrastructure Minister Gregor Robertson, told Reuters in a statement. TRUMP SAYS HE WILL BLOCK US-CANADA BRIDGE UNLESS CANADA NEGOTIATES ON TRADE The bridge was scheduled to open to traffic next Monday, and American and Canadian officials were expected to attend a ribbon-cutting ceremony on Friday, Windsor Mayor Drew Dilkens previously told local media, according to Reuters. Ghassabeh confirmed to Reuters that the bridge will still open next week, but the celebration will be held only "among Canadians." CANADIAN PM CARNEY FIRES BACK AT TRUMP OVER CLAIM THAT 'CANADA LIVES BECAUSE OF THE UNITED STATES' The multibillion-bridge project has faced multiple setbacks amid strained relations between the United States and Canada. In February, Trump threatened to block the project after accusing Canada of unfair trade practices and criticizing its relationship with China. He cited Ontario’s removal of U.S. alcohol products from its liquor store shelves as an example of what he described as unfair treatment. The bridge opening was later cleared to proceed after the U.S. and Canada reached a deal on how tolls would be charged to drivers earlier this month. The new bridge is expected to ease traffic on the privately owned Ambassador Bridge, the largest commercial border crossing between the two countries, which also connects Detroit and Windsor . The port of entry handled $126 billion in trade carried by commercial trucks in 2023, Reuters reported.

title: Woman's remains identified by DNA in Virginia, exposing second alleged murder linked to same 4 suspects
content: The four suspects accused of killing a Virginia teenager are now facing charges in a second homicide after investigators identified a woman whose remains remained a mystery for more than three months, revealing what authorities say were two connected, premeditated killings. Helen Marie Pullen Banks, 56, of Culpeper, was identified through "extensive and complex DNA analysis" completed July 7, after her remains were discovered March 27 on private property in Caroline County, according to the sheriff's office. Authorities announced this month that Rashad Antonio Mayfield, 21, Devonti Gregory Pettaway, 19, Jaden Lamont Phillips, 20, and Kennady Jade Lambert, 18, have each been charged with first-degree murder , conspiracy to commit murder and use of a firearm in the commission of murder in Banks' death. WOMAN FOUND IN SHALLOW GRAVE ID’D AFTER 44 YEARS AS MILLIONAIRE TIED TO ESTATE MURDER PLOT All four suspects were already being held without bond after being charged with murder in the death of 18-year-old Jayden McComber. Investigators say they suspected early in the case that the two homicide investigations were linked. McComber disappeared the same day Banks' remains were discovered. His vehicle was recovered the following day in Virginia Beach with assistance from the Virginia Beach Police Department, according to the sheriff's office. TEENS SUSPECTED OF MURDERING CONGRESSIONAL INTERN LINKED BY DNA ON SHELL CASINGS, PROSECUTORS SAY Authorities said the vehicle was thoroughly processed and produced "valuable investigative leads" that helped investigators locate McComber's remains and identify the suspects. McComber's body was found March 31 in a pond near the Caroline County line. During an April 2 search of a Henrico County residence believed to be associated with Mayfield, investigators recovered personal belongings thought to have been in McComber's possession when he disappeared, authorities said. Mayfield was arrested on charges during a traffic stop conducted while investigators were searching the residence. Authorities said a handgun was seized from his possession, though they have not disclosed whether the firearm has been linked to either homicide. Pettaway, Phillips and Lambert were arrested during a simultaneous operation at an apartment on Kenway Avenue in Henrico. Caroline County investigators were assisted in the arrests by the U.S. Marshals Service Capital Area Regional Fugitive Task Force. MARSHALS NAB TEEN WANTED FOR MURDER OF PENN STATE STUDENT 1,700 MILES FROM CRIME SCENE, 2ND SUSPECT IN CUSTODY Following the arrests, Sheriff Scott Moser described the case as a " complex and difficult investigation " and praised the "relentless work" that led authorities to the four suspects. The sheriff's office said ballistic testing performed with assistance from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives later produced forensic evidence linking the two murders. Investigators say both Banks and McComber knew at least one of the suspects before they were killed. However, authorities said they have uncovered no evidence that either victim had a conflict or dispute with the suspects over what investigators described as "premeditated and deliberate acts." Authorities have not disclosed a possible motive or said whether Banks and McComber knew one another. When Banks' remains were first discovered , the property owner who found them was "understandably shaken" and did not approach the body before calling 911, according to the sheriff's office. "This is a deeply disturbing case," Moser said at the time. "The scene our deputies and investigators encountered was difficult, but they remained focused and professional from the moment they arrived." The sheriff's office later alleged that those responsible had taken "sick and deliberate" measures to conceal Banks' identity, calling it one of the more disturbing cases investigators had encountered. Authorities have not publicly detailed those alleged measures. Banks' identity was formally confirmed July 7, and investigators met with her family that evening to notify them. "This case reflects the relentless commitment of our investigators to pursue the truth," Moser said after announcing the identification. "While no announcement can ease the pain of this loss, we hope today's identification of Helen Marie Pullen Banks provides at least some measure of answers for her loved ones." The investigation has also involved the Caroline County Commonwealth's Attorney's Office, FBI and ATF . Authorities said they are not searching for any additional suspects, though the case remains active. The sheriff's office said Banks' family was notified of her identification on July 7 after DNA testing confirmed her identity. Banks was born in Charlottesville and lived in Rixeyville, according to her obituary. She is survived by five children, her mother, two siblings, 10 grandchildren, one great-grandchild and a large extended family. "Helen was so much more than the circumstances surrounding her passing," her family wrote in a GoFundMe established to help cover memorial expenses. "She was a daughter, a sister, a mother, a grandmother, and a great-grandmother." McComber's family also remembered the 18-year-old in a GoFundMe created after his death, describing the week-long search for him as "a nightmare no family should ever have to live through." "Jayden was so deeply loved," his family wrote. "He had the biggest heart and made sure the people around him knew it. He never missed a chance to say 'I love you,' and those words mean everything to us now." The investigation remains active, though authorities say they are not seeking additional suspects. Fox News Digital has reached out to the Caroline County Sheriff's Office, the Caroline County Commonwealth's Attorney's Office, the Virginia Office of the Chief Medical Examiner, the FBI, ATF, the Virginia Beach Police Department and court officials for additional information.

title: House GOP votes to punt government shutdown battle to after November midterms
content: The House of Representatives voted on Tuesday night to punt the threat of another government shutdown until after the November midterm elections. House lawmakers passed a bill to extend the current fiscal year's funding levels until Dec. 4 via a measure called a continuing resolution (CR). It would extend several weeks into fiscal year (FY) 2027, which begins on Oct. 1. The legislation passed in a 220 to 205 vote. Just six House Democrats supported the measure compared to 204 who voted against. All but one House Republican supported the bill. It's a victory for Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., and House Republicans, who are looking to avoid a messy federal spending fight right before what's expected to be an uphill battle to retain their razor-thin majority. SENATE WEIGHS NEW, PAINFUL LEVERAGE TACTIC AS FEARS OF ANOTHER GOVERNMENT SHUTDOWN GROW House Majority Whip Tom Emmer, R-Minn., the No. 3 House GOP leader, ripped the Democrats who opposed the measure. "As the marxists and communists battle it out for control of the Democrat party, House Republicans are proving yet again that we are the party that governs and works for the American people. Under President Trump’s leadership, we are the party of commonsense. The other side — led by Commie Mamdani —  is the party of chaos and destruction. A majority of Democrats just voted for another damning Schumer Shutdown," he said in reference to New York City's self-proclaimed Democratic Socialist Mayor Zohran Mamdani. The current fiscal year saw the longest government shutdown in history, lasting from Oct. 1, 2025 until Nov. 12, 2025, as Senate Democrats blockaded GOP-led funding priorities for weeks in protest of spending cuts to federal healthcare programs. And Republicans are warning that Democrats would almost certainly cause another government shutdown right before the election if the fight is not punted until after the early November midterms. "Unfortunately, given that Democrats have already forced the two longest government  shutdowns in American history in this Congress, one of them for 78 days, they've already demonstrated they don't care what kind of pain they inflict on the American people," Johnson told reporters on Tuesday. "They've shown there's nothing they'd love more than a government shutdown as tens of millions of Americans head to the polls in November." House Democratic Caucus Chairman Pete Aguilar, D-Calif., told reporters Tuesday that he would vote against the bill along with the top Democrat on the House Appropriations Committee, the panel tasked with overseeing yearly federal spending. "I think that there are some drafting errors within the CR that give Customs and Border Patrol flexibility to move money around. The administration said that all of that was funded within reconciliation 2.0. and I think they're creating other opportunities to transfer funds," Aguilar said. But even with the House's victory, it's not clear that the fight will be over before September. HOUSE GOP PUSHES BACK ON SENATE'S 'SKINNY' PLAN TO END RECORD-BREAKING DHS SHUTDOWN The GOP-led Senate is working on its own course on funding extension, with sources familiar with the process telling Fox News Digital that appropriators were crafting their own CR. They believe the House’s product lacked key extensions to certain programs that are expected to run out of funding come the Sept. 30 deadline. Those programs, known as anomalies, were shipped to the Senate from the White House on Monday. Sen. John Hoeven, R-N.D., a member of the Senate Appropriations Committee, told Fox News Digital that Republicans and Democrats, for the time being, were working together to thwart a shutdown. He hoped to get the CR onto the floor as soon as this week, given that the House is set to leave Washington, D.C., by the end of the week for a long August recess. "Look, we appreciate the House moving forward with theirs. It's, you know, very clean," Hoeven said. "There are just a few issues that we think need to be the rest. Because, obviously, we need to get Democrats on board with us, right now, they're working with us." The move has the full blessing of Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D. "I think it's going to be really important that we figure out a path forward to get a bipartisan agreement to fund the government that will keep government open and ensure that government employees are getting paid," Thune said. "And that is something that I intend to bring to the floor for a vote before the August break.

title: Trump wants FIFA President Gianni Infantino to become the next UN secretary-general: report
content: The close friendship between President Donald Trump and FIFA President Gianni Infantino might become a working relationship. Trump reportedly wants Infantino to be the next secretary-general of the United Nations, per the New York Post. Trump has faith that Infantino is "respected by everyone around the world," and following the first-ever FIFA World Cup in three different countries, the 45th and 47th president of the U.S. believes the world "recognizes he has a special ability to bring people together," a source told The Post. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment by Fox News Digital on this matter. Infantino, the Swiss-born leader of soccer’s largest governing body, grew close to Trump while organizing the World Cup. Trump was included in many different aspects, including Infantino awarding him FIFA’s inaugural Peace Prize back in December. Trump was also seen handing out the Club World Cup trophy last year at MetLife Stadium, and he was present to give Spain’s Rodrì the World Cup trophy on Sunday afternoon at the same venue after Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 to win the tournament. FOX WORLD CUP ANNOUNCER SAYS TRUMP'S APPEARANCE AT FINAL IS 'FUN, UNIQUE THING' DESPITE POTENTIAL BACKLASH During the match, Trump was seated between First Lady Melania Trump and Infantino, while the World Cup trophy was spotted in his suite for viewing prior to handing it out on the pitch. The next secretary-general of the UN will be elected later this year, and that person will begin their post on Jan. 1, 2027. Portugal’s António Guterres will be stepping down come December. Whether Infantino will be considered for the role remains to be seen. He must first be endorsed by all 15 members of the Security Council before receiving confirmation from the General Assembly. The Security Council's five permanent members each have veto power. Infantino must also want the post himself, and it’s unclear whether that is the case here. FIFA did not immediately respond to a request for comment by Fox News Digital. If Infantino wishes to run for secretary-general, The Post learned that Trump believes he would be running against seven "lame" candidates, including Chile's former socialist president, Michelle Bachelet. Argentina’s Rafael Grossi also could be a contender for the role, though the director general of the International Atomic Energy Agency may face resistance from the United Kingdom over the Falkland Islands — a heavily disputed situation between the two countries which found its way into the World Cup . Paolo Zampolli, who serves as Trump’s special envoy for global partnerships, said to The Post Infantino "would do a great job," believing he is "liked by everybody." Zampolli has reportedly dealt with FIFA in the past, as the Italian-American businessman and diplomat pitched to Infantino to replace Iran with Italy for the World Cup in an effort to repair the relationship between Trump and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni. Zampolli was also a former ambassador to the UN for Dominica. "At the United Nations, you have to deal with 193 member states. In FIFA, there are over 200 members [and] Gianni’s great record shows he knows how to manage," he told The Post. Infantino, however, did come under fire by some soccer organizations around the globe after the reversal of Folarin Balogun’s red card for Team USA in the World Cup ahead of their Round of 16 match against Belgium. Trump confirmed he called Infantino for a review of the controversial red card, which would’ve had Balogun, the team’s leading goal scorer at the time, miss the win-or-go-home match. Infantino faces an election of his own next year, as March 2027 will be when the FIFA Congress decides whether he will run a fourth term. Meanwhile, Trump has not shied away from his views about the UN since returning to office, cutting the U.S. contributions to the organization, while pulling out of the World Health Organization (WHO), UNESCO and the UN Human Rights Council. If Infantino doesn't want the post with the UN, and he is re-elected by the FIFA Congress to remain president, he will be organizing yet another tournament in 2027. The FIFA Women's World Cup, which will be held in Brazil, takes place before an even bigger FIFA World Cup in 2030. To honor the 100th anniversary of the tournament, the matches will begin in Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay before the majority of them are played in Spain, Morocco and Portugal. Much like this year's World Cup, history will be made as no tournament has ever been played in six different countries and three different continents. title: Stephen Curry to have a dedicated exhibit at the Basketball Hall of Fame, a 1st for an active player
content: Basketball player Stephen Curry accepts the Muhammad Ali Sports Humanitarian Award at the ESPY Awards in the David H. Koch Theater at Lincoln Center Wednesday, July 15, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Frank Franklin II) 2026-07-21T22:35:12Z SPRINGFIELD, Mass. (AP) — Stephen Curry is headed to the Hall of Fame, making more basketball history with a first-of-its-kind exhibit for an active player. Stephen Curry: Beyond the Arc is set to open Friday, celebrating the career of a two-time MVP and the NBA’s career leader in 3-pointers. The Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame announced the exhibit Tuesday, saying it was the first time in the museum’s nearly 75-year history that an active player would have a dedicated feature experience. “When I think about my journey, I think about the people who believed in me, the work that happened when nobody was watching and the moments that shaped me on and off the court. To have that story told while I’m still playing is something I don’t take lightly,” Curry said in a statement. “My hope is that fans walk through this experience and feel the joy, the purpose and the gratitude that basketball has given me, and maybe see a little bit of their own journey in it too.” Developed in partnership with Curry’s Thirty Ink business team, the exhibit will feature video footage of Curry’s career, memorabilia and audio and video components that tell the story of a player who was overlooked going into college and has gone on to become a 12-time All-Star who led Golden State to four NBA championships. “For him to become the first active player to have an exhibit in the Basketball Hall of Fame is a testament to what he represents to the game, to the Warriors, to the NBA and to his millions of fans around the world,” Warriors general manager Mike Dunleavy said. “Obviously, this is only a prelude to his eventual induction in Springfield, but a fitting tribute to an iconic player and an amazing human being who has single-handedly changed the game.” The Hall of Fame expects Curry’s to be a limited time exhibit, likely to last through the summer of 2027 before closing. ___ AP sports: https://apnews.com/hub/sports

title: 5th person dies in Legionnaires’ disease outbreak in New York City
content:
The exterior of Frank Lloyd Wright's Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum in New York, May 31, 2011. (AP Photo/Kathy Willens, File) 2026-07-22T01:47:32Z NEW YORK (AP) — A fifth person has died in a Legionnaires’ disease outbreak in New York City, health officials said Tuesday night. The New York City Health Department said it has confirmed the presence of the bacteria in 34 cooling towers in 33 buildings, all of which are being cleaned. Officials still haven’t identified the source of the bacteria that has sickened more than six dozen people in the last month. No new patients have come forward with symptoms in the last 10 days, the department said in a news release. Legionnaires’ disease, a form of pneumonia , is treatable but kills about 10% of patients, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. It’s caused by Legionella bacteria, which grow in warm water and can spread in such places as hot tubs and building cooling equipment. People may contract the disease by inhaling contaminated water droplets, but it doesn’t spread person-to-person. Eight people are still hospitalized and 56 others have spent time in but been discharged from hospitals in the Upper East Side outbreak, officials said. The city is cleaning and disinfecting a total of 82 cooling towers in 80 buildings, they said. Inspections have shown that some of the tony neighborhood’s fancy apartment buildings, private schools and renowned museums had traces of Legionella bacteria in their air-cooling equipment — despite new regulations that upped testing requirements just this spring, and despite a budget boost to hire more inspectors. Some owners of buildings that tested positive have said they have worked to stay on top of any Legionella threat. The Guggenheim Museum , for instance, said in a statement that an outside company tests and treats the institution’s cooling tower every month. Read More The situation is avoidable and frustrating, said Jory Lange, a Texas attorney who represents over 50 people who were affected by an outbreak last year that killed seven people and sickened over 100 in New York’s Harlem neighborhood. He’s representing at least three patients who are recovering in the Upper East Side outbreak. “There’s no excuse for this to keep happening,” Lange said. “New York already has the best and strongest regulations … and yet this still keeps happening.” New York City Health Commissioner Dr. Alister F. Martin said in a statement that the department’s quick action after the first two confirmed cases “saved lives.” Martin said the department will learn what happened from the ongoing investigation and update policies and procedures with the goal of preventing future outbreaks. After the Harlem outbreak, city leaders authorized the Health Department in November to hire 23 more Legionella-focused water ecologists and supervisors, bringing the intended total to 56. The staff currently stands at 35, the department said in a statement Tuesday, noting that another 14 people are in a monthslong process of orientation, training and shadowing veteran inspectors. The department said it’s working to fill the final seven positions. Nevertheless, the agency said it did nearly 1,600 cooling tower inspections in the first six months of the year, 35% more than during the same period in 2025.

title: Democrats re-nominate Arizona governor, setting stage for high-stakes November battle
content: Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs cruised to re-nomination in battleground Arizona. That's because the incumbent governor was unopposed in Tuesday's Democratic primary. Hobbs, a former Arizona Secretary of State who narrowly defeated then-GOP nominee Kari Lake four years ago, now heads to the general election in the key southwestern battleground state. "I've never lost an election, but I've also never won one alone. This will be a close race, but I'm excited to be in this fight with all of you to keep Arizona moving forward," the governor told supporters in a social media post minutes after polls closed. DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB Hobbs will face off against the winner of the Republican gubernatorial primary . Rep. Andy Biggs, a former House Freedom Caucus chair, is backed by President Donald Trump and by the political wing of the conservative powerhouse Turning Point USA. Also on the GOP ballot are longtime Republican Rep. David Schweikert, concrete pumping contractor Scott Neely, who's making his second straight run for governor, and business owner Ken Miceli. SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER Hobbs, who has assembled a formidable campaign war chest, spent roughly $7 million during the primary to run ads, even though she faced no competition. "We are running the race we need to win, and it is going to take a lot to get there. We know it's going to be a close race," Hobbs told reporters on Monday. "I'm proud of the support I've garnered and, you know, I'm not raising campaign money to haul it away. I'm raising it to spend." The governor's ads, aimed partially at independent and Republican voters, showcased what she said were Arizona's economic wins during her tenure, and her bipartisan efforts working across the aisle with the GOP-controlled legislature. Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear, chair of the Democratic Governors Association (DGA), said in a statement that "Arizona is always an incredibly competitive battleground and the DGA is all-in to make sure Gov. Hobbs wins so she can continue putting Arizona first." The Libertarian Party, the Green Party, and No Labels are also running candidates on the general election ballot in the race for Arizona governor. Fox News' Olivia Palombo contributed to this story

title: What to know about Pickaxe Mountain, Iran's nuclear site Trump is threatening to strike
content: President Donald Trump has repeatedly issued threats to bomb an under-construction Iranian nuclear site buried deep under a mountain as the two nations exchange blows over the Strait of Hormuz. The site, known as Kuh-e Kolang Gaz La, or “Pickaxe Mountain,” lies on the south side of Iran’s Natanz nuclear enrichment site, which was bombed by the United States during Operation Midnight Hammer in 2025’s 12-day war between Iran and Israel. But Pickaxe Mountain has remained untouched as Iran continues to dig at the site. It remains unclear just what has been placed at Pickaxe Mountain, as the United Nations ‘ nuclear watchdog has never gained access to the site. But Trump on Tuesday talking with journalists in the Oval Office acknowledged the possibility Iran may have moved centrifuges there, potentially at a depth that would challenge even the most-powerful bombs in America’s arsenal. “We’ll be hitting that area … probably pretty soon. And there’s not a thing they can do about it,” Trump said. Here’s what to know about Pickaxe Mountain and the status of Iran’s nuclear program. Pickaxe Mountain site was built after earlier attacks on Iran The new project at Pickaxe Mountain is being constructed next to Natanz, about 225 kilometers (140 miles) south of Tehran, Iran’s capital. Natanz, a mix of above- and underground facilities, has been a point of international concern since its existence became known two decades ago. Repeated sabotage attacks on Natanz, including one likely carried out by Israel that destroyed a manufacturing site for centrifuges, led Iranian officials to start work on the Pickaxe Mountain site. Protected by anti-aircraft batteries, fencing and Iran’s paramilitary Revolutionary Guard, the facility sprawls across 1 square mile in the country’s arid Central Plateau. It has multiple entrances visible from satellite images. In 2023, an Associated Press story on Pickaxe Mountain included analysis from experts at the James Martin Center for Nonproliferation Studies that suggested Iran is likely building a facility at a depth of between 260 and 328 feet. Digging has continued at the site in the time since, with some experts suggesting it could be even deeper underground. Experts say the size of the construction project indicates Iran will likely be able to use the underground facility to enrich uranium as well as to build centrifuges. Centrifuges, tube-shaped devices arranged in large cascades of dozens of machines, rapidly spin uranium gas to enrich it. Additional cascades spinning would allow Iran to quickly enrich uranium under the mountain’s protection. Such underground facilities led the U.S. to create the GBU-57 bomb, also known as a “bunker buster,” which can plow through at least 60 meters (200 feet) of earth before detonating, according to the American military . U.S. officials reportedly have discussed using two such bombs in succession to ensure a site is destroyed. It is not clear that such a one-two punch would damage a facility as deep as the one at Pickaxe Mountain. Trump threatens to bomb Pickaxe Mountain site Speaking alongside Lebanese President Joseph Aoun on Tuesday, Trump initially sought to downplay Pickaxe Mountain by bringing up Iran’s stockpile of highly enriched uranium. Iran had enriched uranium up to nearly weapons-grade levels of 60% before the 2025 strikes. In the time since, Iran is not known to have restarted enrichment and its stockpile is believed to be at still at the bombed enrichment sites. “We follow the material, that’s where the action is,” Trump told journalists. Trump, however, said Pickaxe Mountain was a potential target for American bombers as back-and-forth attacks between Iran and the U.S. rage on. “Normally I wouldn’t say that,” the president added. “If I thought they could do something about it, I would never say that, but we’ll be hitting that area pretty soon. And very heavily.” Iran says that areas around its only nuclear power plant at Bushehr have already come under attack during the war, though no damage was done to its Russian-run reactor. Tehran also said the U.S. attacked the cleared area where it plans to build the Darkhovin nuclear plant, though the U.N.’s International Atomic Energy Agency says there was no atomic material there the last time they inspected the site. The only nuclear power plant in the United Arab Emirates, its four-reactor facility at Barakah, also has been targeted during the war. Iran has since warned that it would take unspecified “required actions” to respond to the Darkhovin attack. Iran’s nuclear program has been a worry for the West for decades In 2025, the U.S. bombed Iran’s nuclear sites at Fordo, Isfahan and Natanz. All three had conducted uranium enrichment. At the time of the 2025 war and the recent Iran war, both Israel and the U.S. said they aimed to stop Iran from ever be able to build a nuclear weapon. Iran has long insisted its program is peaceful, and it isn’t believed by the IAEA or the West to have had an active military nuclear program since 2003. Israel long has been believed to be the Middle East’s only nuclear-armed state. However, even before the recent wars Iranian officials have increasingly threatened to pursue an atomic bomb. The late Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, killed Feb. 28 in the opening moments of the war, issued a verbal fatwa, or religious ruling, that nuclear weapons were un-Islamic. However, his son, Iran’s new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, has not issued any statement regarding his views on the atomic bomb. To build a usable weapon, Iran would first need to enrich uranium up to 90% purity. It would then need to build an actual bomb, and then likely also need to miniaturize it and mount it on a ballistic missile. That process would take months or years, and would face the risk of discovery by Israeli or U.S. intelligence in the meantime.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Franklin Graham visits emergency hospital treating Venezuela earthquake victims
content: FIRST ON FOX: Rev. Franklin Graham visited a Samaritan's Purse emergency field hospital in Venezuela, where doctors and nurses are performing life-saving surgeries and praying with earthquake survivors who have endured unimaginable loss. Graham, president and CEO of Samaritan's Purse and the Billy Graham Evangelistic Association , traveled with his daughter, Cissie Graham Lynch, to encourage relief teams and comfort people who lost loved ones, homes and nearly everything they owned. Lynch, senior advisor and spokesperson for Samaritan's Purse and the Billy Graham Evangelistic Association, said one encounter with a local pastor stayed with her throughout the visit. ARGENTINE SOCCER PLAYER LUCAS TREJO LOSES WIFE, TWO CHILDREN IN VENEZUELA EARTHQUAKE BUILDING COLLAPSE: REPORT "Today, I saw both the immense suffering and the incredible strength of the Venezuelan people," Lynch told Fox News Digital. "I was deeply impacted by the story of a pastor who lost several members of his congregation in the earthquakes and is still serving his community. He said it all when he told us, 'I am here to serve and win souls for Christ.' I thank God for that faithful pastor and for the opportunity that we have to encourage and support him as he shares the hope of Jesus Christ in Venezuela." "These people are surrounded by so much death and destruction. We want to bring the light of Jesus Christ into these places of pain," Franklin Graham told Fox News Digital. "I'm thankful for our incredible teams who are doing just that. They are providing medical care, clean water, tents for shelter, and many other emergency supplies," he continued. "As they do this in Jesus' Name, they are comforting these families and praying with them during this time of intense grief and loss." AMERICANS TRAVEL TO PAKISTAN TO FREE CHRISTIANS TRAPPED IN MODERN-DAY SLAVERY: 'GOD'S HAND WAS IN IT' At the emergency field hospital in La Guaira, medical teams have treated more than 2,500 patients. The hospital includes two operating rooms, a pharmacy and a laboratory, while doctors continue performing orthopedic surgeries and treating infections and other conditions left untreated in the aftermath of the disaster. Two powerful earthquakes measuring magnitudes 7.2 and 7.5 struck Venezuela just 37 seconds apart on June 24, according to the U.S. Geological Survey. The earthquakes killed more than 5,000 people and injured more than 16,000, according to figures announced by Venezuelan authorities. La Guaira was among the areas hardest hit. More than 170 Samaritans Purse Disaster Assistance Response Team members are serving in some of the hardest-hit areas, including La Guaira, Playa Grande and Caraballeda, while aid is also being delivered through church partners in Caracas. PASTOR FREED FROM CHINESE PRISON AFTER TRUMP RAISED HIS CASE WITH XI JINPING Six Boeing 767 airlifts have carried 295 tons of relief supplies into the country. Samaritan's Purse said its aircraft were the first non-military flights to arrive in Venezuela following the earthquakes. More than 10,200 families have received emergency supplies , including tents, tarps, solar lights, blankets, hygiene kits, cooking sets and Spanish Bibles. The organization has also installed four emergency clinic modules for local healthcare facilities, with a fifth expected to open soon. The clinics are stocked with medical supplies and generators to help restore healthcare in communities devastated by the earthquakes. Two desalination units have also produced more than 154,000 liters of clean water. Samaritan's Purse said nearly every patient treated at its field hospital has lost a family member or close friend. Among them was a father who injured his leg while rescuing another person's child from a collapsed 14-story building. "It was terrifying," he said. "I thought a plane had crashed." Another survivor was buried beneath the rubble after his apartment building collapsed, falling six floors and remaining trapped for two days without food, water or light before rescuers spent six hours pulling him to safety. "I lose everything, I don't have anything," he said. "A nurse here made me paper shoes, I feel so happy for that." For the survivor, the compassion and prayer he received proved just as meaningful as the medical care. "The doctors pray with me," he said. "That's beautiful when they get on their knees and pray with me. I love that. Nobody do that for me."

title: Vulnerable Republican wins GOP primary in Arizona toss-up district Dems aim to flip blue
content: Rep. Juan Ciscomani, R-Ariz., clinched the GOP primary nomination in a battleground district Democrats see as key to retaking the House. Ciscomani, a moderate Republican seeking a third House term, ran unopposed with President Donald Trump’s endorsement. The southeastern Arizona district, which spans Tucson's suburbs and stretches to the U.S.-Mexico border, is one of the most hotly contested House races in the country. Trump carried the swing seat by less than 1 percentage point in 2024 after losing it by roughly the same margin in 2020. JoAnna Mendoza, a Marine veteran and political consultant, also ran unopposed in the Democratic primary. She has faced several scandals that could undermine her House bid heading into November. BATTLEGROUND DEMOCRAT SAID TRADITIONALLY WHITE OUTDOOR SPACES 'WILL NO LONGER BE WHITE' The Democrat hopeful has come under recent scrutiny for following several OnlyFans models and self-described witches on her official campaign Instagram account. The sexually explicit accounts included one belonging to a transgender socialist activist who posted pictures in BDSM gear, the New York Post first reported. Mendoza, who is openly bisexual, has also faced GOP attacks after remarks resurfaced from 2020 in which she said she would decriminalize prostitution in response to a question from Equality Arizona, an LGBTQ advocacy group, about the struggles of "trans women of color." "It’s important to ensure that there’s access to the resources, the support networks, the social services, access to healthcare," Mendoza said in the interview, adding, "We need to stop criminalizing people for their situations." 'FLIP FLOP': DEMOCRAT FIREFIGHTER IN TIGHT HOUSE RACE BLASTS POPULAR TRUMP POLICY HIS NATIONAL UNION SUPPORTS "Far-left lobbyist Mendoza is a risk working Arizonans literally cannot afford," NRCC spokesman Ben Petersen said in a statement. Democrats view Mendoza as a strong recruit and have added the political newcomer to their flagship "Red to Blue" candidate program. The nonpartisan Cook Political Report rates Ciscomani’s re-election bid as a "toss-up." Ciscomani, who previously served as a senior advisor to former Gov. Doug Ducey, R-Ariz., and the Tucson Hispanic Chamber of Commerce, is likely to highlight his bipartisan credentials as he seeks a third House term. He is a member of the centrist Problem Solvers Caucus and the Main Street Caucus, which identifies as "pragmatic" conservatives. Ciscomani defeated former state Sen. Kirsten Engel, D-Ariz., by more than 3 percentage points in a 2024 rematch. He first won the seat in 2022, defeating Engel by fewer than 6,000 votes and becoming the first naturalized citizen from Mexico elected to Congress.

title: Rep. Andy Biggs wins GOP primary for Arizona governor
content: Trump-endorsed Rep. Andy Biggs has won the GOP primary to face Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs in November, setting up a marquee governor’s race in one of America’s most competitive states. Biggs, a former chair of the hardline House Freedom Caucus and a close ally of President Donald Trump, easily dealt with his only serious challenger, Rep. David Schweikert, on Tuesday. Before the primary results were official, he had already begun pivoting to the general election against Hobbs, who is seen as one of the most vulnerable Democratic governors this fall. Republicans feel bullish about their odds of flipping the governorship, after Trump carried the state by five points in 2024. But even though Trump won last time, the state has gradually shifted to pure tossup territory over the past few years, electing Democrats to both Senate seats, as well as the attorney general and secretary of state’s offices. Hobbs had already shifted her focus to Biggs as well. Her campaign has amassed a significant warchest for the race and has already started running ads. Biggs, given his lack of a significant primary challenge, has been able to hold onto more cash than his GOP rivals, but is still behind Hobbs. The race will test whether Republicans, who are starting down a potentially bruising midterm cycle, can reclaim the top office of a state that has long been a place of success for the party. During the Republican primary debate, Biggs spent more time talking about his working relationship with House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries and Arizona Democratic Sen. Mark Kelly than he did flexing his endorsement from Trump or highlighting his House record, including his time atop the Freedom Caucus. Instead, he tried to refocus on his bipartisanship in Congress and his leadership in the state legislature. “I know how to reach across the aisle,” Biggs said during the debate. But he will still have to contend with many of his past stances, including his role in trying to overturn the 2020 election . And Hobbs is already working to ensure voters know where Biggs stands on key issues as a longtime member of the House, including his anti-abortion positions and his role in 2020. Her campaign has repeatedly attacked him as “too extreme” for the state and has dubbed him “basement Biggs” for keeping a relatively low profile throughout the GOP primary.

Andy Biggs, a former House Freedom Caucus chair who landed the president's endorsement, captured the GOP nomination for Arizona governor with more than 70% of the vote, the Associated Press announced Tuesday night with just under 50% of the votes counted. Biggs was beating his nearest competitor by more than 50% at that point. DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB Biggs' nearest competitor was Republican Rep. Contractor Scott Neely, who was making his second straight run for governor , had just 7% when the race was called, while business owner Ken Miceli had only 5.4%. Biggs will now face off in the general election with Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs , a former Arizona Secretary of State who narrowly defeated then-GOP nominee Kari Lake four years ago. Hobbs was unopposed as she ran for re-nomination in the southwestern battleground. SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER The Republican primary turned combative and expensive. Schweikert earlier this year went up with campaign mailers accusing Biggs of associating with white supremacist and antisemitic groups. Responding, the Biggs campaign labeled the move as "a desperate tactic by our opponent." Biggs, who was also backed by the political wing of the conservative powerhouse Turning Point USA, mostly ignored his rivals and only joined them on the stage at one of the multiple debates. title: Mark Lamb wins Arizona House primary despite sex scandals
content: A scandal-plagued House candidate powered by President Donald Trump’s endorsement won a messy primary Tuesday. Mark Lamb, the former Pinal County sheriff, overcame a late push from self-funding candidate Daniel Keenan in Arizona’s 5th District. Lamb will enter November as the heavy frontrunner in the deep-red Phoenix-area district to replace Rep. Andy Biggs (R-Ariz.), who is running for governor. Keenan had poured nearly $2 million of his own cash into the campaign and attempted to make Lamb’s alleged sexual misconduct and abuse of power central to the race. Lamb has denied the allegations. But Lamb — bolstered by Trump and Arizona-based Turning Point USA — managed to ward off the attacks. The race’s outcome reveals the strength of Trump’s endorsement, and it’s the latest example of how willing GOP primary voters have been to accept scandal-ridden candidates favored by the president. Lamb, who served as sheriff until 2024, earned national notoriety as a gun-toting critic of the Biden administration’s immigration and border policy. He secured Trump’s backing for the 5th District contest last year. Then in May, the Arizona Republic launched a multi-part investigation alleging that Lamb engaged in a yearslong pattern of sending sexual images and instigating intimate encounters between him, his wife and others. One woman involved, Jillian Stannard, accused Lamb of encouraging her husband to have sex with other women, including Lamb’s wife. She also alleged that Lamb threatened her, saying there would be consequences, when Stannard raised concerns to religious leaders. Screenshots the Republic obtained of messages with another woman, Tammy Peacock, suggest Lamb — then a sitting county sheriff — threatened to leverage Arizona’s revenge porn law against her. In a statement last week, Lamb spokesperson Ed Morabito told POLITICO that “these allegations are false and come from long-discredited political opponents.” Lamb did not lose any significant endorsements in the wake of the scandals — Trump reinforced his endorsement in mid-July — even as Keenan made the allegations central to his campaign.

title: Ex-sheriff backed by Trump storms to victory in race to replace longtime GOP firebrand
content: Mark Lamb, a sheriff with the backing of President Donald Trump , won a GOP primary on Tuesday evening to fill the seat of outgoing Rep. Andy Biggs, R-Ariz., in the Grand Canyon State’s fifth congressional district. The victory puts Lamb on a trajectory to win the seat in November which, in the past, has heavily leaned Republican. Lamb has framed his race as part of a larger effort to protect the cultural fabric of the country, championing "God, family freedom." TRUMP-BACKED NOMINEES DOMINATE PRIMARY CONTESTS AS PRESIDENT TIGHTENS PARTY VICE GRIP "That’s why I’m running for Congress. We gotta make sure our grandchildren and our great-grandchildren have the same freedoms that we have," Lamb said in a campaign video. The seat came open when Biggs, R-Ariz., announced he would run for governor last year. "Arizona has a bright future, but we will need strong leadership to reach its full potential," Biggs said in a press release. "I have been honored to serve Arizona at the state and federal levels and will bring my experience home to my native state to help fulfill its tremendous capacity." The seat is one of the state’s most reliably Republican — and became more so after the state’s redistricting in 2022. Biggs last won reelection in 2024 in a 60.4% to 39.6% victory over Democratic challenger Katrina Schaffner. During his time in office, Biggs was one of Trump’s most prominent backers, pushing for aggressive conservative stances on areas like federal spending and border enforcement . TRUMP-BACKED AIR FORCE VETERAN WINS GOP RUNOFF IN NEWLY-REDISTRICTED HOUSE DISTRICT For his own part, Lamb has echoed many of Biggs’ priorities. "The Joe Biden administration came in, and immediately, overnight, we started seeing hundreds of thousands of people — the majority of these men were military-age men from all over the world. Many of them didn’t love America," Lamb said in a campaign video. "We stood by as our government not only allowed them to come in but rolled out the red carpet for people that broke our law." Lamb’s campaign came under scrutiny earlier this year when an Arizona investigation found that Lamb allegedly had a track record of sending sexual images to women outside of his marriage. Janel Lamb, Mark Lamb’s wife, has called the accusations a political stunt. TRUMP DOESN’T CARE ABOUT THE MIDTERMS? WHY THAT MISSES THE MARK "Politics can be dark and ugly, but if you know us, you know that’s not how we roll. The only way to dispel darkness is not with more darkness, only light. After all we’ve been through, a massive smear campaign is certainly not going to stop us from doing what we know is right," Janel Lamb said in a post to Facebook. Having cleared the primary, Lamb will head to the general election on Nov. 3.

title: Trump-backed Jay Feely wins GOP primary in Arizona’s battleground 1st District
content: Former Arizona Cardinals kicker Jay Feely cruised to victory in Arizona’s 1st District on Tuesday, one of the nation’s most competitive battlegrounds. Feely, a close ally of President Donald Trump, leveraged Trump’s endorsement to topple former state Rep. Joseph Chaplik. He’ll face a steep challenge defeating the Democratic nominee in November: The 1st District, which spans the affluent suburbs north of Phoenix, is one of House Democrats’ top targets after Trump won it by just three points in 2024. Feely is looking to keep the seat under GOP control amid a midterm year that presents major headwinds for the party. During the primary, Chaplik, a member of the Arizona Freedom Caucus, attacked Feely for being insufficiently conservative on gun rights and for his humanitarian work in Haiti . But Feely, one of Trump’s occasional golf partners, leaned on his proximity to the president. “Who can call [Trump] and who can get him to answer? That’s me,” Feely said in a debate. “He will take my call and he will listen. I have the ability to have the ear of the president.” Feely, a former professional football player who counts Tom Brady among his college roommates, first announced his candidacy for GOP Rep. Andy Biggs’ seat in the 5th District. But after Trump backed former Pinal County sheriff Mark Lamb in that race, Feely switched to the 1st District, where he earned the president’s dual endorsement, alongside former state GOP chair Gina Swoboda. "Both fierce advocates of Make America Great Again, Jay and Gina have been with us from the very beginning, and either one would be an incredible Representative," Trump said in January on Truth Social . In February, Swoboda dropped her candidacy for the 1st District and instead ran for secretary of state, leaving the path clear for Feely. As a member of the National Republican Congressional Committee’s MAGA Majority fundraising program, Feely will likely be a top recipient of outside Republican spending in the months leading to November.

title: Los Angeles Angels fired advance scout nicknamed 'Baseball Spy' after he was caught filming Rockies
content: If you're going to torch your baseball career , at least do it spying on a team worth spying on. As first reported by The Athletic, the Los Angeles Angels fired advance scout Justin Prinstein after he was caught filming the Colorado Rockies' coaching staff from the stands during their June series at Coors Field. This story somehow gets even funnier once you learn the details. Prinstein unironically referred to himself as "The Baseball Spy" on social media, and, to reiterate, he threw away his entire professional career spying on the Colorado Rockies . MLB EFFECTIVELY OUTLAWS USE OF AI ON DUGOUT IPADS DURING GAMES Think about that for a second. This wasn't the Dodgers. It wasn't the Yankees. It's a squad more than 20 games behind the division lead. It was the Rockies, a franchise so bad that whatever he filmed probably hurt the Angels more than it helped. Imagine burning down your life's work just to gain an insider edge against a team that barely knows how to play fundamental baseball. According to The Athletic , Prinstein sat in the designated scout section in Denver, pulled out his smartphone, and started recording Rockies coaches in broad daylight. He wasn't using covert equipment à la Conor Stalions. The "spy" was just holding up a cellphone in the middle of a packed ballpark, making him perhaps the least subtle sleuth in baseball history. Someone in the stadium spotted him, notified MLB, and the league office quickly alerted Anaheim. Since the Houston Astros sign-stealing scandal, MLB strictly bans using personal electronics to record coaches or decode signals. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! Former GM Perry Minasian, who was fired in late June, acted fast and fired Prinstein on the spot. Minasian then had to make one of the most embarrassing phone calls of his life, reaching out to Rockies management to apologize for trying to steal secrets from a team that has no secrets worth stealing. MLB concluded Prinstein acted alone, sparing the Angels any fines or lost draft picks. To top it all off, the stolen intel did not even work. The awful Rockies still went out and won two out of three games in the series anyway. Risking your entire career to break MLB rules while spying on Colorado, getting caught immediately, and still losing the series ... the only secret he uncovered was how fast you can get fired.
