title: Long-lost Pan Am crash wreckage found decades after deadly disaster that reshaped airline safety
content: Wreckage was found from a Pan Am flight that ditched in the ocean off Puerto Rico in 1952, a crash that killed 52 people and helped lead to mandatory passenger safety briefings on commercial flights. Searchers recently found the wreckage of the DC-4 by using an autonomous underwater vehicle equipped with high-resolution sonar to locate the fuselage and separated tail in nearly 2,000 feet of water. The Clipper Endeavor aircraft made a hard landing in the ocean after losing engine power shortly after departure from San Juan, Puerto Rico, en route to New York City . The 17 passengers and crew who lived told investigators everyone survived the landing, but many passengers struggled to locate life vests and the crew had a difficult time pulling out life rafts. The plane sank within minutes. FLIGHT ATTENDANTS BEG TRAVELERS TO STOP DOING THE ONE THING THAT ANNOYS CREWS MOST The Civil Aeronautics Board attributed the accident to inadequate maintenance that contributed to the engine failure and to the captain’s handling of the aircraft after power was lost. The panic from the occupants struggling to grab floatation devices helped spur aviation-safety reforms, including mandatory preflight passenger briefings and improvements involving flotation equipment. The crash first drew the attention of Air/Sea Heritage Foundation President Russ Matthews in 2019 when he heard about a luggage tag from the flight washing ashore in Florida and began to dig deeper. This led to years of combing through the Pan Am and Coast Guard archives in search of clues about the location of the plane's wreckage. Reports from the Civil Aeronautics Board, which preceded the Federal Aviation Administration, also aided the search. TRAVELERS REVISIT GOLDEN AGE OF FLYING AS NOSTALGIC COLLECTIBLES MAKE MAJOR COMEBACK However, the key to the wreckage discovery was found in records in Puerto Rico from a hearing held on the crash and a map estimating the site of the crash that was made by Air Force pilots who witnessed the accident because they were in the area on a training flight. Bad weather disrupted a previous attempt two years ago to find the wreckage with a towed sonar array. Matthews said he and his volunteers wanted a second attempt to locate it before next year's 75th anniversary of the crash with a newer advanced drone that was originally created for military uses such as finding undersea mines. Tony Romeo, the CEO of the undersea exploration firm Deep Sea Vision, had been speaking to Matthews for some time about the possibility of helping to find the aircraft if one of his ships was ever in the area. Then in April, one of the company’s ships was passing Puerto Rico between two other jobs while carrying an advanced underwater drone with the right sensors to find the plane. "There we were, and everything kind of came together at the moment: good weather, the right team, and the right equipment and ship. So we took a shot at it," said Romeo, whose father was a mechanic and pilot for Pan Am. Deep Sea Vision previously led an unsuccessful six-month mission in search of Amelia Earhart's plane. All the research Matthews' group had conducted, along with weather data from the time of the crash, was synthesized to develop a map of the most likely location and a search area of 10 square nautical miles. The drone located the wreckage on its first pass over that area, but searchers were unaware until it returned to the surface with images. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

Nomination to Be Arizona’s Top Election Official The New York Times 2020 election denier wins GOP primary for secretary of state in Arizona The Hill Trump, election denialism loom in GOP's secretary of state race azcentral.com and The Arizona Republic

title: ‘It’s a stone around your neck’: Arizona Republicans once again nominate 2020 election deniers
content: To make it out of a Republican primary in Arizona, there’s one key litmus test: believing the 2020 election was stolen from Donald Trump. Election deniers who played prominent roles in efforts to overturn the 2020 results triumphed in statewide Republican primaries Tuesday: Rep. Andy Biggs for governor , state Rep. Alexander Kolodin for secretary of state, and state Senate President Warren Petersen for attorney general. Biggs, a staunch Trump ally who helped try and overturn the election on Jan. 6, 2021, was later subpoenaed in an Arizona probe . Kolodin represented a slate of fake electors, leading to discipline from the Arizona state bar , and filed lawsuits to try to overturn both the 2020 and 2022 elections . Petersen launched a taxpayer-funded audit into Maricopa County’s election system that eventually led to a subpoena. Their victories show GOP primary voters continue to prefer candidates who have pushed false narratives about elections or worked to overturn them. But that can prove toxic in November — and Democrats plan to make their rivals pay for those positions in the fall. "It's one of those things that just won't go away,” said former Rep. Matt Salmon (R-Ariz.). “In the Republican Party in Arizona, in the primary, carrying the Trump line on virtually everything — and that includes election denialism — is still something that benefits you.” But in the general election, “it’s a stone around your neck,” Salmon said. “Among independents and moderate Republicans who vote in the general election, election denialism is not an asset.” Each of the triumphant election deniers Tuesday centered election integrity in their 2026 campaigns. Biggs has been a prominent supporter of the SAVE America Act, the stalled election bill that Trump has pushed repeatedly. Kolodin has advocated for ending Arizona’s permanent early voting list and for stringent ID requirements. And Petersen has pledged to expand the attorney general office’s election integrity unit in order to investigate election results. Arizona was one of the most competitive — and most contested — states in the 2020 election. Fox News’ decision to declare then-candidate Joe Biden’s victory in the state on election night sent shockwaves through Trump’s orbit. It took then-Republican Gov. Doug Ducey several weeks to acknowledge Biden won . The Grand Canyon State became ground zero for Trump’s effort to overturn the election. Trump and his allies pressured Arizona leaders, including then-House Speaker Rusty Bowers, to call the legislature back into session and recall the state’s slate of electors . A group of Republicans falsely posing as alternate electors were later charged with forgery, fraud and conspiracy, a case that is ongoing . Even still, running as an election denier hasn’t been a successful strategy for the Arizona GOP once November rolls around. In 2022, Arizona Republicans nominated hardline election deniers up and down the ballot — Kari Lake for governor, Blake Masters for U.S. Senate, and Mark Finchem for secretary of state — and saw losses in each race, even as Republicans nationally enjoyed an otherwise strong year. And in 2024, Lake again lost, this time for U.S. Senate, even as Trump won the state by more than five percentage points. “Biggs and Kolodin will be saddled with election denialism for the next three months,” said longtime Arizona GOP strategist Barrett Marson. “While Democrats would be wise to focus on affordability, certainly some of their talking points will focus on how these two are dangerous for democracy." Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs, who ran unopposed in the Democratic primary Tuesday and will face Biggs in November, served as secretary of state during the 2020 election. She has portrayed this year’s gubernatorial election as a contrast between confidence and conspiracy in the state’s election system. “Arizona is one of seven swing states that will decide the presidential election,” Hobbs said during an MS NOW appearance Tuesday evening. “If Andy Biggs is governor, Arizona is the first swing state with an election denier in charge, and the time to stop that is not 2028. It is right now.” It’s almost impossible to be a Republican officeholder without agreeing with the president on the 2020 election and the need to dramatically change election law. “As long as Donald Trump, who has the bully pulpit and is the party leader … is talking about election integrity, it will be a top issue in GOP primaries,” said one Arizona Republican strategist, granted anonymity to discuss the issue candidly. “Election integrity measures are broadly popular, but the issue being front and center highlights divisions about Jan. 6th and wasn’t a winning general election issue in 2022,” the strategist continued. “Not sure that general election voters will care much about that in 2026 with such a focus on affordability issues. We are about to find out!” Trump, for his part, has proven unwilling to move past the 2020 election even after winning a return to the White House in 2024. He has never acknowledged he lost that election, and in a primetime speech last Thursday , he announced his administration would declassify documents he alleged show Chinese interference in the 2020 race. “Our elections were left vulnerable to being rigged and stolen, and the trust of the American people was lost,” Trump said Thursday. “This cannot be allowed to continue.”

title: Wednesday briefing: How Trump’s Iran gamble has produced a crisis reshaping the global order
content: In today’s newsletter: ​A White House operating without expertise, strategy or restraint ​is stuck in a conflict with no easy way out, which is sending economic shockwaves far beyond its own borders Good morning. Within two hours of entering No 10 on Monday afternoon, Andy Burnham had his first call with Donald Trump. After chit-chatting about the football (both agreed England had an “excellent tournament”) and Manchester (our new prime minister invited the president to visit the city Trump once described as a “town”), they got on to far trickier territory: the strait of Hormuz. The US has attacked Iran for the eleventh consecutive night, hitting aircraft hangars and drone storage sites across the country. It came after Iran launched retaliatory strikes on US air bases and neighbouring Gulf states, which have accused it of deliberately targeting desalination plants that are essential to life in the region. Each side now claims it is preventing the other from gaining control over the strait of Hormuz, through which 20% of the world’s oil was shipped before the war began. Vessels carrying crucial shipments of oil, gas and fertiliser remain at a standstill. UK politics | Andy Burnham is under mounting pressure to explain how he will pay for his policy pledges as he implored his new cabinet to examine “all possible ways” to tackle the cost of living crisis. UK news | A man has appeared in court charged with the murder of the former MP and Reform UK spokesperson Ann Widdecombe. Joshua Kerry, 28, is accused of killing the former Conservative minister at her home in Haytor, Devon, by hitting her on the head with a hammer 21 times. Middle East | The US defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, told the Senate the US-Israel war on Iran had cost $37.5bn so far , as he faced lawmakers furious over the conflict’s soaring price tag and the deaths last week of three American service members. Climate crisis | About 23 million people will be banned from using hosepipes by this weekend, as England and Wales moves closer to drought status . content: Two Democratic candidates remained locked in a battle as of early Wednesday morning to claim their party’s nomination in Arizona’s 1st Congressional District for a chance to face former NFL kicker Jay Feely. Former television news anchor Marlene Galán-Woods and former state Rep. Amish Shah, the two frontrunners, fell shy of capturing enough of the vote to win the nomination outright by early Wednesday morning. The winner of the primary will go on to have a rare opportunity to flip a seat in the Canyon State and, more broadly, potentially decide the balance of power in Washington, D.C. TRUMP-BACKED FIREBRAND WINS ARIZONA GOP GOVERNOR PRIMARY, SETTING UP HIGH-STAKES SHOWDOWN The seat could very well decide whether Republicans hold on to a slim majority in the House of Representatives or whether Democrats break a Republican governing trifecta come the November midterms . Although the district has favored Republicans since 2020, incumbent Rep. David Schweikert, R-Ariz., has only narrowly hung on to the seat in the past two cycles, beating out Shah in a 51.9% to 48.1% victory in 2024. Schweikert announced that he would not pursue reelection last year, announcing that he would instead pursue a gubernatorial bid . Trump-backed Rep. Andy Biggs, R-Ariz., won his primary and was ahead of Schweikert by over 50 points early Wednesday. VULNERABLE REPUBLICAN WINS GOP PRIMARY IN ARIZONA TOSS-UP DISTRICT DEMS AIM TO FLIP BLUE "I’ve grown to believe Washington is unsavable. I do believe Arizona is savable," Schweikert told Axios. This isn’t the first time Amish Shah and Marlene Galán-Woods have competed against each other for their party’s nomination, having clashed in the Democratic 2024 primary for the district. At that time, Shah narrowly defeated Galán-Woods before advancing to the 2024 general election, where he lost to Republican Rep. David Schweikert, who has represented the Phoenix-area seat since 2013 despite Democrats investing heavily to flip the district blue. HOUSE DEMOCRATS' CAMPAIGN ARM DRAWS PROGRESSIVE FURY FOR TRYING TO 'TIP THE SCALES' IN KEY HOUSE PRIMARY He is seeking a second consecutive nomination after arguing he remains the strongest candidate to challenge Feely in the general election. Galán-Woods, meanwhile, is expected to emphasize her background as a longtime Arizona television journalist and her ability to appeal to independent and suburban voters. Galán-Woods is making another bid for the nomination with support from several national Democratic organizations, which view Arizona's 1st District as one of the party's best pickup opportunities in 2026. The winner will go on to the general election on Nov. 3.

title: DHS issues $84B in fines to illegal immigrants under Trump administration
content: FIRST ON FOX: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has issued more than 100,000 civil fines totaling roughly $84 billion to illegal immigrants under the Trump administration while collecting more than $1 billion in payments, Fox News Digital has learned. Since President Donald Trump returned to the White House about 18 months ago, DHS has issued 103,000 civil fines totaling approximately $84 billion, a DHS official told Fox News Digital. As of July, the agency had collected about $1.2 billion in fine payments. TRUMP PUTS ASYLUM LAWYERS ‘ON NOTICE’ WITH NEW FRONT IN WAR ON FRAUD Shortly after Trump's return to office, the administration announced it would begin fining illegal immigrants subject to final removal orders $998 per day if they failed to voluntarily leave the United States or otherwise comply with their removal orders. Illegal immigrants are required to pay the fines before they are deported, and DHS has said it may seize assets from those who fail to pay. The Trump administration has unveiled a series of measures designed to encourage illegal immigrants to leave the country, including DHS' announcement that those who refuse to self-deport could face "significant financial penalty." DHS has argued the program costs significantly less than traditional deportation proceedings and is designed to encourage illegal immigrants to voluntarily leave the United States. TRUMP ADMINISTRATION ORDERS GREEN CARD APPLICANTS TO LEAVE THE US, APPLY FROM THEIR HOME COUNTRIES U.S. Customs and Border Protection released a flyer outlining the "benefits" and "consequences" for illegal immigrants who self-deport using the CBP Home app. "Self-deportation is safe," the flyer stated. "Leave on your own terms by picking your departure flight." According to DHS, non-criminal illegal immigrants who voluntarily leave the United States may keep money they earned while in the country and preserve eligibility to pursue legal immigration in the future. Some may also qualify for subsidized flights if they cannot afford travel home. TOM HOMAN WARNS ICE SURGE COMING TO NEW YORK CITY AS MAMDANI BOASTS ABOUT SANCTUARY STATUS Meanwhile, the flyer warns that those who fail to self-deport will be "apprehended by DHS with no opportunity to get your affairs in order beforehand." In May, Fox News Digital reported that more than 3 million illegal immigrants had left the United States during Trump's first year back in office, according to figures provided by DHS. The department said an estimated 2.2 million of those migrants self-deported. DHS also said the administration had deported nearly 900,000 illegal immigrants and arrested more than 900,000 others as of May 17. The department said the figures demonstrate that Trump's immigration crackdown has reshaped migration patterns following a record number of illegal crossings during former President Joe Biden's administration. Fox News Digital's Brittany Miller and Landon Mion contributed to this report.

title: Rubio says US remains open to Iran talks but warns there 'will be consequences'
content: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday that the United States remains willing to negotiate with Iran but warned there "will be consequences" if Tehran continues to violate its commitments. Speaking at the ASEAN Summit in the Philippines, hours after U.S. forces completed their 11th consecutive night of strikes against Iranian military targets, Rubio said Washington remains open to diplomacy but questioned whether Iran is negotiating in good faith. "The problem we're having right now is they're not serious about talks. If they're serious, we're serious," Rubio said. "If they're not, then we will do what is necessary to protect our interests and also the interests of our allies." STEVE FORBES URGES TRUMP TO KEEP THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ OPEN AT ALL COSTS Rubio said Iran has demanded the right to control shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, arguing Tehran has no legal authority to do so and warning that allowing it would set a dangerous international precedent. "If we create a precedent in the Middle East where a nation-state can decide that they are going to control an international waterway and, if you don't pay them, blow up your ships, we have created a very dangerous precedent, which will repeat itself in other parts of the world, including in this region," Rubio said. Rubio argued the "fundamental principle of freedom of navigation" is at stake. US CLAWS BACK KEY CONCESSION TO IRAN AFTER FRESH ATTACKS ON COMMERCIAL SHIPS IN STRAIT OF HORMUZ "If that is threatened, then I think the global economy is threatened, and the rules which have underpinned 150 years of international trade and commerce are also threatened, and that cannot be allowed to happen," he said. Rubio's comments came after the U.S. and Iran passed the halfway point of the 60-day negotiating window established under a June 17 memorandum of understanding covering Iran's nuclear and missile programs, sanctions and freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. Despite the agreement, the two countries have appeared closer to a broader conflict than a diplomatic breakthrough, with Iran repeatedly attacking commercial vessels in the strait while U.S. forces continue striking Iranian military targets across the region. TRUMP'S 60-DAY IRAN DEAL REACHES HALFWAY MARK AS CEASEFIRE COLLAPSES INTO ESCALATING WAR While President Donald Trump has declared the ceasefire "over," he said Tuesday that Iran wants to "desperately meet." Rubio echoed the president's remarks, saying Washington remains prepared to negotiate while making clear military force remains an option. "The United States remains open and willing to engage in positive negotiations and talks so long as the commitments that are made are kept," he said. "When those commitments are not kept, which is what’s happened in this particular case, then there will be consequences. And that has to happen." Rubio said maintaining the threat of military action is necessary to prevent Iran from disrupting one of the world's most important shipping lanes. "If these consequences didn't exist, then today we would be living in a world where a significant percentage of the energy supply in this region and 20% of the world's energy supply is being held hostage by a rogue regime," Rubio said. Fox News Digital's Morgan Phillips contributed to this report.

title: Trump flexes GOP muscle in Arizona primaries as Dems dodge far-left upset
content: President Donald Trump’s sway within the GOP was on display in Arizona’s primaries Tuesday night, as his endorsed candidates powered through key Republican contests while Democrats avoided a far-left upset in one of the state’s House races. But Trump’s influence in Republican primaries was the top storyline of the night, with his endorsed candidates powering through key contests up and down the ballot. Rep. Andy Biggs, a former House Freedom Caucus chair who landed Trump’s endorsement, easily captured the GOP nomination for governor, topping Rep. David Schweikert and the rest of the Republican field by over 50 points. Meanwhile, former NFL kicker Jay Feely, who received Trump’s "complete and total endorsement" in the final stretch, also won the GOP primary in Arizona’s competitive 1st Congressional District. TRUMP-BACKED FIREBRAND WINS ARIZONA GOP GOVERNOR PRIMARY, SETTING UP HIGH-STAKES SHOWDOWN Former Pinal County Sheriff Mark Lamb, another Trump-backed candidate, won the GOP primary in Arizona’s 5th Congressional District, the deep-red seat Biggs is vacating to run for governor, and Trump-backed Juan Ciscomani advanced in Arizona's 6th Congressional District after running unopposed. Biggs’ win sets up a high-stakes general election against Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs, who cruised to renomination after running unopposed in the Democratic primary. Hobbs, a former Arizona secretary of state, narrowly defeated then-GOP nominee Kari Lake four years ago and now heads into a second-term fight against one of Trump’s most prominent allies in Congress. The race in Arizona's 1st Congressional District, where former NFL kicker Jay Feely came out victorious in the GOP primary Tuesday night, is a rare open seat contest as Schweikert, who has held the seat but gave it up to run for governor, created an open-seat battle in the suburban Arizona district. The Phoenix-area district includes northeastern Maricopa County and large parts of Scottsdale, Paradise Valley and Fountain Hills. Feely now moves into a general election fight, where he is expected to face former state Rep. Amish Shah, who was up by almost nine points early Wednesday morning. The Associated Press hadn't called the race as of 3 a.m. Wednesday. EX-NFL STAR BACKED BY TRUMP WINS BATTLEGROUND STATE PRIMARY: 'TRUE AMERICA FIRST CONSERVATIVE' Lamb’s win in Arizona’s 5th District gave Trump another victory in a reliably Republican seat and positioned the former Pinal County sheriff to replace Biggs in Congress. Lamb, who has campaigned on "God, family, freedom" and echoed Biggs’ hard-line border message, heads into the general election as the favorite in a district that heavily leans Republican, even after his campaign faced scrutiny earlier this year over allegations involving inappropriate messages to women outside his marriage. While Trump-backed Republicans powered through their primaries, Democrats avoided a potentially damaging left-wing upset in Arizona’s 4th District, where Rep. Greg Stanton held off progressive challenger Kai Newkirk. Newkirk challenged Stanton from the left, making the race a test of whether the left-wing energy that has shaken Democratic primaries elsewhere could break through in Arizona. Stanton’s win blunted that narrative, at least for one night, and spared Democrats from having to defend a more polarizing nominee in a battleground Sun Belt district. The result gave establishment Democrats a needed win after a cycle in which progressive challengers have increasingly pressured incumbents over issues including Israel, ICE, healthcare and corporate influence.

title: Andrés Cantor's top calls from the 2026 World Cup
content: The 2026 FIFA World Cup delivered and met all expectations, with 104 games full of energy, emotion, athletic prowess and stadiums full of colorful, intense crowds cheering for their national teams. One big part of the allure of the tournament was the play-by-play performance of legendary Telemundo broadcaster Andrés Cantor. He is one of the most recognizable voices in soccer, with his likeness appearing in commercials and even “The Simpsons.” 2026 World Cup Jul 16 Ranking the top goals from the 2026 World Cup: Messi, Mbappe, Cape Verde on list 2024 Paris Olympics Aug 3, 2024 WATCH: Snoop Dogg learns how to do soccer commentator Andres Cantor's famous goal call Cantor followed his native Argentina and the United States , his adoptive homeland, throughout the World Cup, as well as a couple of Canada and Brazil games and the debut of Curaçao. Here’s a list of some of Cantor’s best goal calls during the World Cup. 7. First USMNT goal in the opener against Paraguay The first goal for the U.S. men’s national team came after an amazing play on the left side by American forward Christian Pulisic and a ball misplayed by Paraguay’s Damián Bobadilla, who beat his own goalie. The USMNT had its best performance of the tournament with a 4-1 win, destroying the Paraguayan defense , one of the best in South America. 6. Curaçao scores its first goal in World Cup history Curaçao made it to the World Cup for the first time in its history, and Livano Comenencia scored for the tiny Caribbean island in the 21st minute of its opener against powerful Germany. In the end, the four-time world champions crushed Curacao 7-1 , but the joy and the emotion of that first goal was one of the moments to remember from this World Cup. 5. Lionel Messi kicks off the scoring in Argentina’s opener vs. Algeria The 2022 world champions had their first match against Algeria. It was a tough one until Lionel Messi grabbed a ball in the center lane and delivered a left-footed scorcher that beat goalie Luca Zidane, the first of three goals from Messi in the game . Messi, who turned 39 years old on June 24, went on to score eight goals in the tournament, second only to France’s Kilian Mbappé, who scored 10 . Throughout his career, the Argentinian has scored 21 goals in six World Cups. 4. Folarin Balogun puts the UMSNT on the board against Bosnia and Herzegovina Forward Folarin Bolagun scored the last of his three goals in the World Cup against Bosnia and Herzegovina , as the first half of the USMNT’s game in the first knockout round was about to expire. The USMNT won 2-0, but the game will be remembered forever as Balogun was sent off in the second half. After the game, President Donald Trump asked FIFA President Gianni Infantino to reconsider the one match suspension of the U.S player, and Balogun was allowed to play against Belgium in the Round of 16. 3. Ferrán Torres scores to secure World Cup title for Spain The Spanish team had a near perfect tournament that ended with seven wins and one tie, a surprising one in its first game against tiny Cape Verde. “La Roja” overpowered Argentina in the final game and a goal by Ferrán Torres in extra time was enough to allow the Spaniards to lift the World Cup trophy for the second time in history . 2. Enzo Fernández seals Argentina’s comeback victory over Egypt In the round of 16, the powerful Argentinian team had been surprised by Egypt and was trailing 2-0 with a little more than 10 minutes left of regular time. Led by Messi, Argentina scored three goals, the last one by Enzo Fernández in stoppage time , to advance to the next round of the tournament. Cantor’s call of Messi’s equalizer against Egypt was equally thrilling. 1. Lautaro Martínez’s header stuns England in the semifinals In an epic game, reminiscent of the one played at the 1986 World Cup in Mexico City, Argentina came back to beat England with two goals near the end of the match . Enzo Fernández tied the game with a shot from outside the penalty area in the 85th minute, and Lautaro Martínez’s header sealed the victory for Argentina in the 92nd. Both on assists by Messi to send the team to its second straight World Cup final. And finally, it was not in this World Cup, but how can we forget Cantor’s goal call that went viral after Gonzalo Montiel scored the decisive goal in the penalty shootout to allow Argentina to beat France and win its third World Cup in 2022 in Qatar ? title: As the president touts Trump Accounts, some families are still waiting for baby's $1,000
content: President Donald Trump says Trump Accounts could hoist children out of poverty and give more Americans the chance to benefit from investments in the stock market. But some parents say they’re still waiting for the money to arrive. Trump on Wednesday plans to speak at a Georgia high school to promote the investment accounts, which offer $1,000 in seed money to every child born during his second term. The accounts went live July 4 , two days before Trump rang the opening bells for both the New York Stock Exchange and NASDAQ from the Oval Office. The tax-advantaged accounts, created last year through Trump’s signature One Big Beautiful Bill, can be opened for any child under the age of 18. The Treasury Department boasts 6.5 million sign-ups for Trump Accounts , with 1.5 million of those eligible for the $1,000 seed funding for babies born from 2025 through 2028. Boosters of the program say it’s a chance to give more Americans a stake in the stock market. They hope it will stem the rising popularity of democratic socialists, who seek to raise taxes on corporations and the wealthy to ease the cost of things like food and healthcare for low-income and middle-class Americans. After the Trump Accounts are set up, parents, relatives, friends and employers can contribute to them. Some billionaires have also pledged philanthropic contributions . The money is turned over to private firms that invest it in index funds, a type of mutual fund that tracks the performance of the stock market. The money can’t be accessed until the child turns 18, and only then for specific purposes, such as going to school, opening a business or buying a home. For babies born since Trump took office last year, $1,000 from the U.S. Treasury is supposed to kick off the accounts. While some parents report receiving the money, others said in interviews and on social media they’re still waiting for the accounts to receive $1,000. Masaki and Kristina McLellan, new parents from Bergen County, New Jersey, said in an interview they were wary of signing up for the accounts because they worried it was a promotional stunt for the president. But the $1,000 incentive persuaded the couple, whose daughter Maya was born in late March, to start an account anyway. Masaki McLellan said he applied for the account July 6. At first, the application was rejected, but the account was activated after he spent an hour on the Trump Account hotline. He was told he’d see the money in the account in 10 days. Now, he says, he’s been told it will take up to four weeks. Kristina McLellan said she was disappointed it was taking so long to fund her daughter’s account. But the infant has multiple other investments already compounding for her. Maya’s parents have already started a 529 college savings plan and a custodial brokerage account for her. The Trump Account is the third investment account in the little girl’s name. “We definitely want to give her options for her future and make sure she can choose what she wants to do,” said McClellan, a studio director for a local news station, who returns from maternity leave next week. The Treasury Department said the lag between opening an account and receiving the seed funding constitutes “standard processing time, like receiving a tax refund” and that the overwhelming majority of parents are only waiting one to two days. But the department likes to give parents a conservative estimate for how long it might take for the money to be transferred, such as the estimate of up to four weeks given to the McLellans. “Trump Accounts level the playing field by allowing every parent to invest in their children’s future, not just wealthy families with trust funds,” the department said. “With roughly 1 million sign-ups per month before launch, Trump Accounts have become the most popular and successful government-backed savings product in U.S. history.” Trump’s stop in Georgia comes as he and fellow Republicans face pressure in the midterm elections for their handling of the economy. Only 33% of U.S. adults approve of Trump’s economic leadership, among the lower ratings of his second term, according to a June survey by The Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research. Trump pledged to lower costs, but his tariffs and the war in Iran have instead helped to increase prices. Trump Accounts are similar to “baby bonds,” championed by Democratic-led cities and states meant to shrink the wealth gap between low- and high-income children. But unlike most baby bonds, which generally target kids from disadvantaged backgrounds, Trump Accounts are available to families of all incomes. The program has faced criticism from those who say it does nothing to help families in a child’s first years of life, when children are most likely to experience poverty, homelessness and hunger. And the bill that created the program, the president’s signature One Big Beautiful Bill, also slashed funding for programs that are disproportionately used by children, including Medicaid and the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program. ___ Associated Press writer Adriana Morga contributed to this report.

title: STEVE FORBES, STEPHEN MOORE: America must free its airwaves before China pulls ahead
content: Washington rarely discovers an economic policy that promotes investment, strengthens national security, improves services for consumers and raises billions of dollars for the Treasury without imposing a new tax. Federal Communications Commission Chairman Brendan Carr’s newly announced "super band" spectrum auction manages to do all four. Spectrum may be invisible, but it is among the most valuable resources in the modern economy. It carries phone calls, financial transactions, emergency communications, industrial data, streaming video and the growing volume of information moving between connected devices. The FCC has moved to auction 160 megahertz of the Upper C-band — the valuable mid-band airwaves that provide the combination of speed, capacity and geographic reach required by modern wireless networks. AMAZON LEO SATELLITE INTERNET TAKES ON STARLINK Congress directed the commission to make at least 100 megahertz available. The FCC went further, adding another 60 megahertz and combining it with spectrum cleared in 2020. The result will be a contiguous block of more than 400 megahertz, creating one of the most commercially useful bands of wireless spectrum in the world. This will be the first major federal spectrum auction in five years . The commission also moved from a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking to a final order faster than it has in any comparable proceeding during the 5G era. That urgency is welcome. STEVE FORBES: REGULATORS RISK DESTROYING LOCAL TV BY BLOCKING KEY MEDIA MERGER Keeping usable spectrum idle — or trapped in inefficient government allocations — has real costs. Networks aren’t built. Jobs aren’t created. New services don’t reach consumers. American companies lose ground to foreign competitors. Auctions offer the quintessentially American solution: Free up and use markets. A properly designed auction gets spectrum to companies that value it most and are prepared to put it to productive use. It establishes clear, enforceable rights. It encourages private investment. And it generates revenue for the federal government without raising anyone’s income, payroll or capital-gains taxes. COULD THE NEXT CHINESE THREAT WALK INTO YOUR KITCHEN ON TWO BATTERY-POWERED LEGS? The economic potential is enormous. The FCC estimates that putting this spectrum to work could add as much as $264 billion to gross domestic product, support 1.5 million jobs and create nearly $390 billion in benefits for consumers. Those estimates may sound ambitious, but history shows the value of these airwaves. The first C-band auction in 2000 raised roughly $81 billion for the federal government. Few government actions can promote economic growth, encourage lower consumer prices and reduce federal borrowing at the same time. This one can because it relies on competition rather than command-and-control regulation. The auction is also a national security imperative. The country that leads in mid-band spectrum will have an enormous advantage in 5G, the emerging 6G economy and the artificial-intelligence, robotics, transportation and defense applications that depend on advanced connectivity. Wireless leadership isn’t merely about downloading movies more quickly. It determines which country’s companies develop the next generation of network equipment, whose technical standards are adopted internationally and where the investment and high-paying jobs associated with these technologies are created. China understands this. Beijing has long treated spectrum as a strategic national asset. It has deployed extensive mid-band capacity, built networks at enormous scale and used subsidized telecommunications equipment to increase its influence around the world. America’s regulatory apparatus, by contrast, has often moved at the speed of an old rotary telephone. The Upper C-band order is crucially important, but it can’t be a one-time event. America badly needs a long-term spectrum strategy, not the haphazard, hit-and-miss approach we’ve had up to now. Wireless companies and technology innovators make investment decisions years in advance. They need a predictable pipeline of licensed spectrum, not occasional auctions that are interrupted by political disputes and bureaucratic delays. Washington should establish a multiyear calendar that identifies which bands will be studied, cleared and auctioned. Congress should also make the FCC’s auction authority permanent. Allowing that authority to expire, and then reviving it through temporary extensions, creates uncertainty and delays investment. No successful business would manage one of its most valuable assets that way. Neither should the U.S. government. Washington must also take a harder look at the enormous amount of spectrum controlled by its own agencies, including the Defense Department. National security operations must be protected. But "national security" shouldn’t become a mantra that prevents officials from examining whether every allocation is being used efficiently. There are effective ways to preserve government capabilities while freeing additional spectrum for commercial use. The big problem is that federal agencies have little incentive to surrender unused and/or unneeded airwaves. Congress should change that by allowing agencies to share in the savings or auction proceeds generated when they consolidate operations, upgrade equipment or relinquish underused spectrum. The broader principle is straightforward. Government shouldn’t attempt to build wireless networks, dictate business models or select favored technologies. Its responsibility is to free scarce spectrum, establish clear rights, enforce the rules and then get out of the way. Private capital and American ingenuity will do the rest. Chairman Carr’s Upper C-band auction follows that formula. But technological leadership isn’t secured with a single auction. Washington must adopt a sensible, long-term strategy so that America has the spectrum resources required to dominate the next technological era. Stephen Moore is a co-founder of Unleash Prosperity and a senior fellow at the America First Policy Institute.

title: China is building a massive ship that should scare Americans about the future
content: An enormous vessel taking shape near Guangzhou, China, appears designed to refuel, rearm and resupply Chinese carrier groups far from home. At roughly 885 feet long, it could become the world’s largest dedicated naval replenishment ship. Every Army officer learns the same lesson: weapons attract attention, but logistics decides who can stay in the fight. The ship does not prove that war is imminent. It does, however, fit a larger pattern. China is building the physical, industrial and technological capacity to absorb economic punishment, replace battlefield losses and project power long after a crisis begins. Taiwan remains the most dangerous flashpoint, but Beijing is preparing for a contest that could continue well beyond the opening shots. CHINA’S IRAN TIES COMPLICATE TRUMP-XI SUMMIT AS TENSIONS TEST US LEVERAGE Energy is the first requirement of endurance. By late February, China held an estimated 1.2 billion barrels of onshore crude, enough to cover roughly 109 days of seaborne imports. Those stocks gave Beijing more room to absorb the oil-market shock created by the Iran war. Beijing is extending its military reach as well. The Pentagon says China is developing a global logistics and basing network that could include permanent bases, shared facilities, military sites beside commercial infrastructure and temporary access to foreign ports. A joint logistics center opened at Cambodia’s Ream Naval Base in April 2025, while China continues to explore access along the sea lanes through the Malacca Strait, the Strait of Hormuz, Africa and the Middle East. THREE KEY REASONS WHY AMERICA CANNOT AFFORD TO LOSE TAIWAN TO COMMUNIST CHINA Beijing is building the ships that carry power and the access network that keeps them supplied. China’s advantage is not confined to ships already afloat. It has built an industrial system able to manufacture and repair them. A U.S. Trade Representative investigation found that China’s share of global shipbuilding tonnage rose from less than 5% in 1999 to more than 50% in 2023. Commercial orders sustain the workers, steel mills, dry docks and suppliers that also strengthen the Chinese navy. TIM SHEEHY EXPOSES A 'SCARY' SHIPBUILDING COLLAPSE THAT LEAVES THE US VULNERABLE TO CHINA The same pattern is visible in the air. The Royal United Services Institute estimates that production of the upgraded J-20 stealth fighter reached about 120 aircraft a year by late 2025. An open-source assessment places the total delivered by mid-2026 at roughly 500. The exact number matters less than the lesson: China can mass-produce a sophisticated combat aircraft once dismissed as experimental. On July 6, a Chinese nuclear-powered submarine launched a long-range ballistic missile into the Pacific. Whatever Beijing’s characterization, the test demonstrated greater sea-based nuclear reach and complicated any American calculation about intervening in a regional war. China is not simply buying a military. It is building the means to replace one after losses begin. Modern weapons depend on minerals, chips and data. The International Energy Agency reports that China is the leading refiner for 19 of 20 strategic minerals it tracks, with an average market share of about 70%. Those materials feed batteries, power grids, jet engines, electronics and defense systems. In a long confrontation, control over the ingredients needed to build the next missile may matter as much as the missile already in the launcher. Beijing is shrinking its semiconductor vulnerability too. Chinese companies held 33% of global production capacity for foundational logic chips in 2023, up from 19% in 2015. These are not the most advanced chips, but they are workhorses inside vehicles, industrial equipment, communications systems and many weapons. Advanced computing power fits inside this strategy too. At the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai, Xi Jinping promoted Chinese open-source models, training for developing countries and a new coalition called the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization. Beijing wants Chinese technology and standards embedded across the Global South. Space ties these systems together. The U.S. Space Force says China ended 2025 with more than 1,353 satellites in orbit, including more than 510 capable of intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance. Those systems improve Beijing’s ability to locate American carriers, track deployed forces and support long-range targeting. China’s Cross-Border Interbank Payment System now has 210 direct participants and 1,619 indirect participants. It does not replace the dollar; the renminbi accounted for only 1.99% of reported global currency reserves in the first quarter of 2026. Its purpose is more practical: keep essential trade moving if Western financial channels are restricted. The campaign also reaches inside the United States. In June, the Justice Department and FBI disabled 13 websites allegedly backed by Chinese intelligence personnel. The sites posed as consulting businesses and targeted current and former U.S. officials and military personnel, especially security-clearance holders. Investigators said the operation used computer-generated profile photographs, professional networking sites and online payments to appear legitimate. China is preparing to sustain power abroad while seeking leverage inside the societies most capable of resisting it. Beijing has serious weaknesses. China’s population fell by 3.39 million in 2025. Its property slump continues to depress confidence and domestic demand. The People’s Liberation Army has not fought a war since 1979 and lacks extensive modern combat experience, and the renminbi remains far from challenging the dollar. Those weaknesses do not disprove the strategy. They explain why Beijing is building buffers. Xi understands where China is vulnerable and is methodically reducing those vulnerabilities before a major crisis. Washington still treats shipbuilding as a Navy issue, semiconductors as a Commerce Department issue, minerals as a trade issue, espionage as an FBI issue and Taiwan as an Indo-Pacific Command issue. Beijing sees one contest. America must do the same. We need larger stockpiles of munitions and strategic materials, sustained investment in shipbuilding and repair, secure allied supply chains, hardened space and communications networks, and deeper coordination with Japan, Australia, South Korea, the Philippines, Taiwan and Europe. We must also warn current and former officials about Chinese recruitment methods without treating Chinese Americans as suspects. The giant vessel near Guangzhou may never dominate a television broadcast. It lacks the drama of a missile launch or a stealth fighter crossing the Taiwan Strait. But it may tell us more about China’s plans than either. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION Xi is building a country capable of fueling its forces, replacing losses, protecting industry and operating beyond the reach of a quick American knockout. China is preparing not only for a battle, but for the long contest that follows. The urgent question is whether America is doing the same. Nations that lose that race rarely get to run it twice. Beijing is spending every year of American hesitation to build its advantage. Washington still has time to close the gap, but not much of it remains. CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM ROBERT MAGINNIS

title: SENATOR TIM SHEEHY: Crazy conspiracy theories are undermining America’s defense
content: The National Defense Authorization Act has long been one of the few pieces of legislation that rise above politics, typically culminating in a bipartisan show of support for our military and national defense . Each year, Congress comes together to fund our military, equip our warfighters and make clear to our adversaries that the United States remains committed to peace through strength. This year, however, that tradition came to an end. Instead of debating how best to strengthen America's military, Democratic Socialists and online conspiracy theorists are choosing political theater over national security. One provision of the FY27 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) in particular – Section 1217, which establishes the United States-Israel Defense Technology Cooperation Initiative – became the target of a misinformation campaign fueled by rising antisemitism and growing domestic hostility toward American power and influence on the world stage. THE US-ISRAEL STRATEGIC ALLIANCE – PARTNERSHIP, NOT CHARITY According to the groypers and far-left socialists behind this delusional campaign, Section 1217 somehow "merges" the U.S. military with Israel's, places American troops under foreign command and subordinates America's national security to another country's interests. While this sounds like a great plot for a novel, none of it is even remotely true. Section 1217 builds upon decades of intelligence sharing, defense research and technology cooperation between the United States and Israel to accelerate the development of capabilities that strengthen America's military. "Section 1217 merges our militaries." No, it does not. Section 1217 does not alter America's constitutional chain of command. It does not place a single American service member under Israeli authority. This claim isn’t simply inaccurate – it’s absurd. And frankly, it doesn’t make one iota of strategic sense. Israel's security challenges are largely regional, as it fights to defend itself from hostile neighbors who seek every day to wipe the Jewish people off the map. America's military responsibilities span every continent and ocean, maintaining a global force capable of deterring China in the Indo-Pacific, defending NATO allies in Europe, protecting freedom of navigation and responding to terrorist threats wherever they may be. MAMDANI’S ‘DERANGED’ ISRAEL TAKE RESURFACES AS HE TARGETS NETANYAHU Neither nation has any interest in "merging" military commands because it would make both countries less effective, not more. Section 1217 isn't some secret, nefarious scheme buried in the NDAA as the anti-Israel lobby would have you believe. It's a continuation of a defense partnership that has benefited our warfighters for decades. For years, Israel has fought radical Islamic terrorists and hostile regimes while pioneering advances in missile defense, counter-drone technology, cyber defense, battlefield intelligence and autonomous systems. America benefits from this knowledge, just as Israel benefits from American industrial capacity, research and military leadership. As a combat veteran, I’m familiar with a concept every warfighter understands: on the battlefield, you use every advantage available to protect your troops and accomplish the mission. Pride and bad-faith political symbolism don’t win wars. Superior technology, trusted allies and military dominance do. That is exactly why Congress included Section 1217 in this year's NDAA. Artificial intelligence, cyber warfare, autonomous systems and electronic warfare are no longer tomorrow's technology; they are deciding battles today. In Ukraine, inexpensive drones have destroyed tanks worth millions of dollars. In the Middle East , missile defense systems have intercepted massive barrages that would otherwise devastate civilian populations. MORNING GLORY: AMERICA IS WINNING ITS BATTLE WITH IRAN. IT’S ONLY A MATTER OF TIME Our adversaries aren't working alone. China invests heavily in artificial intelligence, autonomous weapons, quantum computing and next-generation military technology with one goal: overtaking the United States. Russia continues adapting through battlefield experience. In this age of modern warfare, America cannot afford to handicap itself by refusing to work with trusted allies while our enemies freely share tactics, technology and capabilities. The anti-Israel crowd tries to suggest Section 1217 somehow places Israel's interests above America's. That could not be more backwards. The provision puts our interests first with every technological breakthrough, every missile defense improvement and every advance in counter-drone capabilities that saves American lives. That's not charity – it’s security. As Montanans, we understand the importance of preparedness. Our state has long played a vital role in America's national defense, from Malmstrom Air Force Base to the generations of veterans who have worn our nation's uniform. We know deterrence isn't built with speeches, but with capability, credibility and a military so advanced that our enemies decide not to test it. Americans should absolutely debate foreign policy . We should debate defense spending, military priorities and America's role on the world stage. But these days, legitimate policy disagreements have been replaced with tired antisemitic tropes dressed up as national security concerns. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION Let’s be clear: conspiracies about Jewish control of America's military have no place in a serious debate about our nation's defense. Our enemies don't care whether the technology that defeats them was developed in Washington, Tel Aviv, or on the far side of the moon. They care that it works. We have a responsibility to ensure American warfighters have every possible advantage when they go into harm's way – not to try and score political points by spreading disgusting conspiracy theories. Section 1217 does just that by making America stronger, our military more capable, and our adversaries less likely to challenge us. That's peace through strength. CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM SEN. TIM SHEEHY

title: The battle for Congress gets a Wall Street-style scoreboard powered by real-money bets
content: EXCLUSIVE: As the race for control of Congress heats up, prediction markets are emerging as an increasingly influential complement to traditional polling, offering real-time election forecasts that shift as news breaks and campaigns evolve. The launch reflects a broader shift in how elections are being tracked. Unlike traditional polls that capture voter sentiment at a single moment, prediction markets update continuously as traders react to debates, fundraising, endorsements and breaking news, giving campaigns and political observers a real-time read on how races are evolving. Kalshi launched its new Midterms Hub on Tuesday, bringing together live market odds, polling averages, fundraising data, historical election results and political news into a single dashboard tracking House, Senate and gubernatorial races. Kalshi said it plans to expand the platform beyond the 2026 midterm elections , with the goal of making it a permanent destination for tracking U.S. political races. PREDICTION MARKETS FAVOR DEMOCRATS IN NEW YORK, NEW JERSEY, VIRGINIA ELECTION DAY RACES "Prediction markets don't care about spin or partisanship," Tarek Mansour, Kalshi's co-founder and CEO, said ahead of the launch. "They cut through polarization and show you what the wisdom of the crowds actually believes, backed by real money, not rhetoric." The company argues that it gives users a more dynamic view of the campaign than traditional polling alone. "You're able to see things happen in real time," a Kalshi spokesperson told Fox News Digital, arguing prediction markets can capture shifts in momentum that periodic polling may miss. Kalshi says the platform has evolved beyond a trading venue, with roughly 75% of visitors using it to monitor election forecasts rather than place trades. A spokesperson said that trend suggests many users view the markets as an informational resource, even if they never place a wager. FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS: VOTERS SAY THEY'RE IN ECONOMIC PAIN, BUT WILL DEMOCRATS GAIN? As election markets have grown in popularity, they've also sparked debate over whether traders with nonpublic political information could gain an advantage. Kalshi says it is federally regulated in the United States, where insider trading and market manipulation are illegal, and that it monitors its markets for suspicious activity. The hub allows users to track races by competitiveness, projected party flips and trading volume while viewing polling averages, Federal Election Commission fundraising reports and historical voting results. Users can also see how election odds have changed over time following debates, fundraising reports and other major campaign developments. Beyond voters and political observers, Kalshi says campaigns can use the hub to gauge whether debates, endorsements, fundraising hauls or breaking news are shifting expectations in real time instead of waiting days for new polling. Kalshi says candidates favored by its markets have won about 90% of races since 2024, even three months before Election Day.

title: Trump, Rubio don't plan to stop Tate brothers' extradition to the U.K.
content: President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio aren't planning to block the extradition to the U.K. of the Tate brothers, the notorious "manosphere" influencers accused of rape and human trafficking. Why it matters: Andrew and Tristan Tate were part of the coalition of hyper-masculine social media voices advocating for Trump when he was reelected in 2024. The brothers have reported connections to two of Trump's sons and have had support from top Trump advisers. Officially and publicly, Trump and his administration have kept the Tates at arm's length because of their sordid reputations. "The U.S. has an extradition treaty with the U.K. and the administration intends to honor it in this case," a senior administration official told Axios. Driving the news : U.S. marshals arrested the Tates in Miami on Saturday after British authorities issued 38 new sex-crime charges against the brothers, bringing the total combined counts against them to 59. They also were indicted on separate sex-crime charges in Romania in 2023. Zoom in: In court filings, the Justice Department made clear that Rubio has "sole discretion" to block their extradition to the U.K. if he believes the brothers are being politically persecuted. On Monday, Tate attorney Joe McBride told reporters outside the federal courthouse in Miami that the charges against the two are "politically motivated. There's no question about it." McBride said the brothers are innocent and will fight extradition. A senior State Department official told Axios that "the secretary has not spoken to the Tate Brothers or their lawyers. The State Department has no plans to act on this matter at this time." Behind the scenes: Those who know Rubio's thinking say the secretary, a conservative Catholic who fought as a U.S. senator for stronger human trafficking laws and protections for victims, isn't inclined to help the Tates. "Marco thinks these guys are scum," said one source. "Now if the president overrules him, which I don't think is likely, he's got a problem." A source familiar with Trump's thinking said the president wants nothing to do with the brothers. "The Tates want to pretend they were responsible for the president's victory [in 2024], but they weren't part of our strategy and the president doesn't know them," a former Trump campaign adviser said. Flashback: After Andrew Tate first faced rape allegations in the U.K. in 2015 the brothers moved to Romania, where they began running their online porn business, according to a damning long-form investigation by the New Yorker called "Andrew Tate's Empire of Abuse." When Trump won his first election in 2016, Andrew Tate posted supportive MAGA tweets and began messaging the president's oldest son, Donald Trump Jr. Tate's online profile grew amid a masculine backlash to the 2018 #MeToo movement. His online courses sought to teach young men how to profit from turning women into "sex slaves," and awarded "PhD's" that stood for "Pimpin' Hos Degree." As criminal investigations into the Tates grew, the brothers drew a parallel with the "lawfare" that Trump said he faced while running for reelection in 2023. During that time, Andrew Tate sat for softball interviews with podcasters Tucker Carlson and Candace Owens. Trump gave a Truth Social shoutout to Tristan Tate. After an assassination attempt on Trump in 2024, Andrew Tate told reporters, "I'm very close with the Trump family. I know them well." He said he spoke with Trump's youngest son, Barron, and called the president "a bulletproof badass." The intrigue : A month after Trump returned to office last year, Romanian authorities reinstated the Tate brothers' right to travel outside of the country as prosecutors reexamined procedural issues with their case. Romania's foreign minister denied that the decision was linked to pressure from a Trump adviser, Ric Grenell, who had spoken favorably of the Tates. Grenell told Axios the minister broached the topic of the Tates with him and he made no demands. Shortly afterward, the Tates flew from Romania on a private plane to Fort Lauderdale, Fla., where Customs and Border Patrol officers seized their phones. The Tates got their phones back, however, thanks to the intervention of their former lawyer, Paul Ingrassia, who then was a White House liaison to the Department of Homeland Security, according to Pro Publica . Ingrassia told Axios the report was inaccurate. Inside the room : Last week the Tates were in D.C., where they met with some members of Congress and rubbed elbows with insiders at the exclusive club, The Ned. There, they ran into Trump confidant and special envoy Paulo Zampolli, the Daily Mail first reported . Zampolli invited the Tates to join 150 guests at his July 15 "summer soiree" at Zampolli's Dupont Circle home. Zampolli told Axios he'd met the Tates three times before, starting at the Milken Institute Global Conference this year in Los Angeles, where he sat for a friendly interview on Andrew Tate's podcast . "I did not know these allegations about them," Zampolli said. "That is on me." What they're saying: One attendee at Zampolli's party said it was attended by people from the Justice, State and Treasury departments, as well as D.C. insiders and even some World Cup soccer players. "The Tate brothers were like celebrities. People wanted to take pictures with them," the source said. "You never would've known they were about to get arrested."

title: ‘Cannot rule out foul play' after independent autopsy for Nolan Wells, attorney says
content: An independent autopsy could not “rule out foul play” in the mysterious death of Nolan Xavier Wells , an 18-year-old who disappeared after a Fourth of July boating trip with friends before his body was found floating in the water near the Mississippi island they ventured to. The preliminary findings were made public during a news conference held at the annual NAACP National Convention in Chicago by civil rights attorney Ben Crump, who is representing the family. The examination, Crump announced, did not determine a cause or manner of death, but did note some “significant” findings. Among the notable findings, according to Crump, was a “discoloration in the soft tissue of the back of the head, the occipital region,” though no underlying skull fractures or lacerations to the skin around the area were found. The report showed no evidence of fractures or bruising, but the decomposition of the body, along with other limiting factors, made it impossible to make a determination. “[Dr. Roger Mitchell] talked about how he found red discoloration when he cut open into the back of his head towards the occipital bone, and he saw the red discoloration, and we actually saw the pictures of it. It’s significant,” Crump said. But the pathologist noted that certain organs, which were removed during the initial autopsy conducted by the Mississippi State Medical Examiner’s office, were “absent” from the body. “He said it is assumed that the initial pathologist retained these structures for additional evaluation,” Crump said. While not an uncommon practice, Crump said the organ removal posed “several limitations during the second autopsy that create barriers to establishing a definitive cause and manner of death for Nolan Xavier Wells.” “In cases where a death has occurred in or around a body of water with suspicion of drowning, it is important to confirm how that person entered the water. This is the crux of the matter,” Crump said. “This information is especially important for those deaths of persons who can swim, as in the case with Nolan Wells. At the time of this report, this forensic pathologist does not know the condition of Nolan Wells. He did not know whether he was conscious or unconscious when he entered the water. He said that would be significant. He said he did not know whether he was forced into the water or unforced into the water. He said that would be significant … He said definitive circumstances of death are required to determine the manner of death. For these reasons, this pathologist cannot rule out … if any intervening non accidental factors contributed to or caused the death of Nolan Wells. “Understand, he said based on the examination of the body, he cannot rule out foul play,” Crump said. “That is significant.” Crump had previously vowed to conduct his own investigation into the circumstances of the teenager’s disappearance, which followed a July 4 boat trip with friends to an island off the coast of Mississippi. Wells did not return to the mainland with his friends. His body was found floating off the island’s coast two days later. The Mississippi State Medical Examiner’s Office conducted its own autopsy but has yet to release the results. The second autopsy was arranged by the family and Crump, and paid for by former NFL player Colin Kaepernick. Crump said it would determine if Wells “had any physical injuries to his body beyond drowning.” The still-unknown circumstances around Wells’ death have touched off rampant online speculation and prompted calls from Black leaders for transparency from local authorities. Wells, who was Black, had traveled to the island with a group of high school friends, all of whom are white. A reward of $125,000 — jointly funded by the Rev. Al Sharpton, actor and producer Tyler Perry and former NFL player Terrell Owens — is now being offered in exchange for information leading to an arrest and conviction in connection with the death. The autopsy announcement comes two days after Wells was laid to rest in his hometown of Ocean Springs, Mississippi . Mississippi Jul 20 Hundreds gather for Nolan Wells' funeral in Mississippi Mississippi Jul 10 Investigation underway into death of Mississippi 18-year-old who vanished on July 4 boating trip In his eulogy, Sharpton lamented the “inconsistencies and unanswered questions” that had placed a dark cloud over the grieving family. He questioned why Wells’ friends had left him behind, taken his phone and keys and failed to report him missing to police. And he suggested local investigators had spoken prematurely in statements to the press indicating that no crime was suspected. “The reason that a lot of people across the nation are looking at this Nolan situation is because we’re looking at the history in Mississippi,” Sharpton added. “We can’t have someone in law enforcement saying there was no foul play before there was an investigation.” Jackson County Sheriff John Ledbetter said initial interviews suggested Wells chose to stay on the island and that his friends believed he would get a ride with someone else. He has said the friends were cooperating with the investigation, which remains ongoing. “We are trying to be respectful and collaborative as much as we can,” Crump said. “But it’s always troublesome to all of us when these investigations just take forever.” This story uses functionality that may not work in our app. Click here to open the story in your web browser.

title: Family speaks out after mother, toddler killed in fiery, high-speed San Jose crash
content: In every photo on the Balistreri family’s wall, you see a smiling Ivana and her daughter, Lilly, a toddler who hadn’t yet turned 2. Now, the family is speaking out about the fiery December crash on Highway 87 in San Jose that took their lives, hoping to share their grief and serve as a cautionary tale for the community. The Santa Clara County District Attorney’s Office has filed two counts of murder against the driver who struck them, Zachary Chernicky. Prosecutors allege he was driving more than 100 mph when he hit the family’s vehicle. An attorney representing the family said data from Chernicky’s car shows he had been driving more than 140 mph at times. The fatal collision occurred on Dec. 2 of last year. Ivana, Lilly, and Ivana’s fiancé, Zachary Martins, were on Highway 87 when traffic came to a halt. Martins was behind the wheel. “We were at a full stop,” Martins told NBC Bay Area. “I looked in my rearview mirror and I literally thought, is he gonna stop?” Chernicky did not stop. NBC Bay Area reviewed previously unreleased video of the incident. Following the high-speed impact, Martins jumped out of the burning car, desperately trying to save his fiancée and daughter. “Yeah, it’s blurry and vivid at the same time,” Martins said of his rescue attempts. “I was concussed and running off adrenaline.” Ivana and Lilly died inside the burning vehicle. San Jose Jul 17 Driver was going over 140 mph before double-fatal crash in San Jose, DA says San Jose Jul 16 CHP arrests driver in deadly 2025 crash on Highway 87 in San Jose San Jose Dec 4, 2025 ‘Absolutely shattered': Family mourns woman, child killed in fiery Highway 87 crash The pain remains raw for the victims’ extended family. “They were rays of sunshine,” said Francesca Alexander, Ivana’s sister. “Ivana did not have a mean bone in her body. She was always very kind, very open.” Ivana’s mother, Benedettea Balistreri, mourned the loss of her granddaughter. “My little Lilly,” she said. “She was my sunshine.” Aurelio Balistreri, Ivana’s father, said the crash shattered their entire family. “He destroyed my life, my kids’ life, my wife’s life,” he said through tears. “Every morning I get up out of bed thinking about Zach not having his babies. That’s on my mind every day.” For Rosie Balisteri, Ivana’s sister, navigating the grief requires balancing overwhelming emotions just to make it through the day. “It’s hard,” she said. “Trying to hear her in my mind to go work out, go on a run or do something. But I just want to lie in bed and not do anything, so it’s just trying to find a balance and trying to keep her memory.” When asked about the possibility of forgiveness for the man accused of killing his family, Martins was resolute. “When we saw him in the courthouse, there was the tiniest, little microscopic piece of me that felt slightly bad for him cause I know prison is hell; it’s probably worse than death,” Martins said. “But then I got home and I realized I’m in [expletive] prison every day…I don’t think I ever will be [ready to forgive].” Benedettea echoed the desire for strict accountability. “I just want justice,” she said. “I just want the person responsible to spend the rest of his life in prison and think about what he did.” Through their heartbreak, the family is sharing their story with a singular hope: preventing another tragedy. “We just really want to bring attention to it, to make a plea to the community to slow down and think about getting home safe, the next person getting home safe, so we don’t have to go through something like this,” Alexander said. NBC Bay Area reached out to Chernicky and his attorney for comment but did not hear back.

title: FOX reports massive, record-shattering ratings for 2026 FIFA World Cup Final between Spain and Argentina
content: Ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup , many doubters around the world and within sports media, claimed that the United States would be a disastrous host. That hosting the tournament under President Donald Trump would mean fewer international visitors, and that the U.S. shouldn't host because soccer was still a niche domestic sport. And surprise, surprise, turns out those concerns were completely invalid. Attendance broke records before the end of the group stage. Visitors flowed into the U.S. from around the world, then gave glowing reviews to their hosts, stadiums, and local fans. Some were even overcome with emotion at the kindness they experienced in the country. TRUMP ADMIN TAUNTS LEFT FOR ‘PRAYING’ FOR WORLD CUP DISASTER AS DOT TOUTS RECORD NUMBERS The other concern? That fans wouldn't watch? Turns out that could not have been wrong. Already, in the round of 16, the match between the U.S. Men's National Team and Belgium set records for the most watched English language broadcast of a soccer game in the history of the country. The World Cup Final, however, featured two teams that have little connection to the United States: Spain and Argentina . Yes, Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal added star power, but rosters on both sides did not rise to the level of familiarity most have with say, France or England. And yet, Tuesday afternoon, FOX reported that ratings and viewership blew that USMNT-Belgium game out of the water. The network announced that Spain-Argentina drew a whopping 38.937 million viewers, peaking at nearly 52 million. That shattered the record for most-watched English-language soccer broadcast in the country's history. UNITED STATES-BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA WORLD CUP MATCH DELIVERS MASSIVE TV RATINGS Not only that, but it represented the highest viewership for a non-Super Bowl sporting event since the Winter Olympics in 1984. That's remarkable, and it shows how far soccer has come in the United States, and how interest in the World Cup has surged. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM It also raises the possibility that the U.S. should be considered a bit of a rotating host for the tournament. If the field expands to 64 teams, as expected, few other countries have the existing infrastructure to host that many games in large stadiums. And growing the sport in the U.S. is a key goal for FIFA. Just imagine how high those numbers would be in a 2038 tournament, if the USMNT could go deeper into the tournament. Even reaching a World Cup final. Hopefully, we won't have to imagine it.

title: Sausalito's city manager makes first court appearance since arrest
content: Sausalito’s city manager made her first court appearance Tuesday since her arrest last weekend. Elaine Forbes, the newly-hired city manager for Sausalito and longtime former director of the Port of San Francisco, faces misdemeanor charges of unlawful lodging, petty theft and prowling. Yacht captain Bill Aubrey discovered Forbes barricaded aboard the Lisa Marie at the Sausalito Yacht Harbor early Saturday morning after hearing her repeatedly blow the horn. He got in the vessel through a window and found Forbes barefoot and acting strange. “She just looked at me, put a smile on her face and said, ‘Good morning,'” Aubrey said. “And I said, ‘Good morning to you. How’s your day going?’ And she goes, ‘Good.’ And I said, ‘Why don’t you just have a seat right here?'” Aubrey called police, who said they had been looking for Forbes for days. She had been reported missing last week. Andy Cunningham said Forbes had been on board her boat, too. Cunningham said Forbes left it completely ransacked. “She pretty much ransacked the whole thing with clothing, jewelry, glassware, alcohol, salt, cherries, maraschino cherries,” Cunningham said. “She basically made a complete and utter disaster of the whole boat, throwing things this way and that.” Forbes was wearing Cunningham’s clothes when she was found and arrested, Cunningham said. sausalito Jul 20 Sausalito leaders to discuss city manager's job after arrest, charges sausalito Jul 19 Sausalito city manager arrested while on leave Sam Singer, a Forbes family spokesman, said Forbes was suffering a mental health crisis. “Elaine had a mental breakdown,” Singer said. “She believed that she was on her boat, not somebody else’s boat.” Singer said Forbes is now hoping to get the help she needs. He said she wants to stay behind bars for now. “Elaine and her family are working to get counseling,” Singer said. “They’re speaking with a variety of different providers. They’re speaking with her attorney and they’re going to get her on the right path because she is a beloved, respected Bay Area public servant.” Forbes is scheduled to be back in court on Wednesday.
